title: npm run test:package can never pass: README tool inventory regex, packed tool list, and contract fingerprint are stale
description:
## Evidence
`npm run test:package` (last step of `npm run check`, and the CI installer-package job on ubuntu + macOS) fails deterministically at scripts/package-smoke.mjs:504: `README tool inventory differs from tools/list` (documented 37 vs advertised 39). README.md uses one combined heading `#### \`save_svg\` and \`save_png\`` which the regex `/^#### \`([^\`]+)\`$/gm` (package-smoke.mjs:501-506) cannot match.

After patching that in a scratch copy, `expectedPackedToolNames` (package-smoke.mjs:70-107) also lacks save_svg/save_png, and after fixing that the packed contract fingerprint check (package-smoke.mjs:950-966) fails: `Packed tool contract fingerprint differs: 6c24f2e8…` (pinned e0853089…). The CI "Test installer" step is skipped on every run because it follows this failure.

## Impact
The release gate is red for every commit; the only test of the tarball, installed bin, and CJS bundle never completes; the installer suite has never run in CI on either OS.

## Fix
Split the README heading into two (or accept multi-tool headings), add both names to expectedPackedToolNames, regenerate the contract and workflow fingerprints from current tools/list, and add an in-process test that runs the inventory check so `npm test` catches drift. Run test:package to completion before tagging.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 33g.10: the README heading, the packed tool list and the pinned fingerprints all derive from a generated scripts/tool-contract.json refreshed by 'npm run contract:update'; an in-process test catches drift without a pack cycle; two stale geometry baselines were re-pinned to the diagnostics the imperfect fixture genuinely produces, and the corrected-collaboration baseline is now empty because the workflow's own repair resolves the semantic error. npm run test:package passes end to end. 33g.13: version set to 0.3.0 across package.json and both plugin manifests, with a dated CHANGELOG section covering the five undocumented commits and all 12 previously unmentioned tools; nothing was tagged. 33g.14: README examples capture and reuse returned element IDs and state the real Mermaid-derived IDs; both were replayed against a live server.

title: CI has never been green: e2e 'drains an active SVG render' times out on GitHub runners and swallows the real error
description:
## Evidence
GitHub Actions ci.yml: 9 of 9 recorded runs failed, including latest main (run 32692937172) and this branch (run 33885584239). In the quality job (Node 22.12 and Node 24): `✕ drains an active SVG render and closes its browser process (22379 ms)` / `Timed out waiting for /tmp/mcp-bpmn-render-exit-e2e-…/browser.pid at waitForFile (tests/e2e/server.test.ts:232:9)`. Because test:all chains `&& npm run test:e2e:compiled && npm run test:renderer && npm run test:installer`, the renderer suite and the 1120-line installer shell suite have never executed in the quality job.

The sibling schema test passes on the same runner because it isolates HOME and falls through to /usr/bin/google-chrome; the failing test launches Puppeteer's managed Chrome for Testing with no launch args (src/core/BpmnSvgRenderer.ts:397-420); Ubuntu 24.04's user-namespace restriction breaks its sandbox. The test discards the real error (`await render.catch(() => undefined)`, tests/e2e/server.test.ts:646) and never prints server stderr.

## Impact
The documented gate is permanently red; regressions in the 809 in-process tests, e2e, renderer, or installer are indistinguishable from the standing failure.

## Fix
Include stderrBuffer + tool result in the thrown error; set PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/google-chrome in CI or add a browser-args override (see the --no-sandbox bead) and use it in CI; add branch protection on `check`.
close_reason: Fixed and confirmed green. CI run 33896102710 on b24ce5f is the repository's first successful run: Node 22.12 quality gate, Node 24 quality gate, and the installer/package jobs on ubuntu and macOS all pass. Fixes: the renderer accepts MCP_BPMN_BROWSER_ARGS and adds --no-sandbox under uid 0, the workflow sets that flag, and the e2e drain test now throws the real tool result plus server stderr instead of a bare marker timeout. Two regressions found and fixed while verifying: regenerating the lockfiles from scratch on Linux dropped 24 @esbuild platform binaries and fsevents, which npm 11 on Node 24 rejects; and the dependency overrides pushed npm audit onto the retiring quick-audit endpoint, which returned 'Invalid package tree'. Both resolved by advancing fast-uri and qs within their existing declared ranges. Branch protection on the check job remains a repository setting the maintainer must enable.

title: auto_layout fails on any diagram containing a tool-authored text annotation
description:
## Evidence
Fresh process -> add_text_annotation {text:"Note"} -> auto_layout returns isError=true: `Error: Layout output changed BPMN semantics`. Reproduced via MCP stdio (3-node process + one annotation).

Root cause: addTextAnnotation stores properties {"text":"Note"} (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:577-580) but re-importing the layout XML through moddle yields {"text":"Note","textFormat":"text/plain"} (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:2281-2284). The post-layout semantic snapshot compares element.properties verbatim (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2960-2989) and throws. Passing textFormat:"text/plain" explicitly, or close+open_bpmn before layout, works; adding another annotation after reopen fails again.

## Impact
The skill's canonical flow ("add annotations, then auto_layout", skills/bpmn-modeler/references/workflows.md:13-14, SKILL.md step 9) fails with an opaque error whenever an annotation exists. Release blocker.

## Fix
Default textFormat to "text/plain" in addTextAnnotation (or normalize the snapshot the same way isExpanded is handled). Make the snapshot mismatch error name the element and field that differ. Add a regression test: annotation + auto_layout succeeds.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. a3j.8: the post-layout semantic snapshot now applies bpmn-moddle's textFormat default to both sides (SimpleBpmnEngine.comparableElementProperties) so an authored annotation compares equal to the same annotation read back, and the rejection names the differing field. a3j.9: waitForCompletion is deleted rather than assigned undefined, since moddle serializes any own property. Tests: SimpleBpmnEngine.test.ts annotation-layout cases, compensation cases, and a guard asserting no BPMN attribute is ever the literal "undefined".

title: Compensation event definitions serialize waitForCompletion="undefined" (schema-invalid XML)
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:1331 `definition.waitForCompletion = payload.waitForCompletion;` runs unconditionally; when the agent omits the optional field, moddle serializes the JS undefined. Reproduced via MCP: add_event intermediate-throw compensation with activityRef, and add_event end compensation, export xml ->
```
<bpmn:compensateEventDefinition id="CompensateEventDefinition_1" waitForCompletion="undefined" activityRef="Task_1" />
<bpmn:compensateEventDefinition id="CompensateEventDefinition_2" waitForCompletion="undefined" />
```

## Impact
waitForCompletion is xsd:boolean; the file is schema-invalid. Camunda 7 deployment and XSD-validating tools reject it. Every diagram with a compensation throw/end event created without an explicit waitForCompletion is affected, and `validate` does not catch it because bpmn-moddle parses leniently.

## Fix
Assign only when `typeof payload.waitForCompletion === 'boolean'`, otherwise leave unset. Add a contract assertion that the attribute is absent or true|false.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. a3j.8: the post-layout semantic snapshot now applies bpmn-moddle's textFormat default to both sides (SimpleBpmnEngine.comparableElementProperties) so an authored annotation compares equal to the same annotation read back, and the rejection names the differing field. a3j.9: waitForCompletion is deleted rather than assigned undefined, since moddle serializes any own property. Tests: SimpleBpmnEngine.test.ts annotation-layout cases, compensation cases, and a guard asserting no BPMN attribute is ever the literal "undefined".

title: Prevent new_bpmn from silently overwriting an existing diagram after restart
description:
## What / impact
`new_bpmn` and Mermaid import autosave to a deterministic filename derived from a process ID and diagram name. `IdGenerator` starts over in every server process, while `commitMutation` defaults to `overwrite=true`. Creating the same-named first diagram after a restart silently replaces the prior file and destroys user data. This is a prerelease blocker.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Point two fresh server/engine instances at the same empty temp diagrams directory.
2. In the first, create a named process, add a task, and stop all state.
3. In the second, create the same name/type and compare IDs, filenames, bytes, and reopened elements.

## Evidence
Two fresh `SimpleBpmnEngine` instances pointed at one temp directory both generated the same process ID and filename. The second `new_bpmn` returned success; reopening that file showed the second empty diagram and the task from the first was gone (`sameId:true`, `sameFilename:true`, `overwritten:true`). Mermaid conversion also resets generator IDs, making equivalent collisions predictable.

## Where
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:100-115, 797-848, 1057-1085, 1298-1308
- src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts ID reset/import path
- src/utils/IdGenerator.ts
- src/utils/FileManager.ts:228-256
- handlers for new_bpmn/new_from_mermaid/open_mermaid_file

## Implementation direction
Do not use process-local counters as persistent file identity. Generate collision-resistant root IDs/filenames or atomically reserve a unique default filename. Make initial creation no-clobber and surface a bounded conflict error; only an explicit, separately validated overwrite operation may replace an existing file. Preserve transactional memory/disk adoption if reservation fails.

## Verification
Add a temp-directory integration/e2e test that creates a populated diagram, disposes/recreates all server state, creates the same name/type again, and asserts the original bytes/elements remain plus a distinct second file. Repeat for new_from_mermaid and concurrent same-name creation. Run persistence, handler, e2e, and package checks.
acceptance_criteria: A new diagram never replaces an existing file unless the caller explicitly opts into overwrite; restart/counter reset cannot collide; a regression test proves the first file is byte-for-byte unchanged and both diagrams remain listable; save_as keeps its no-clobber semantics.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: added UUID-backed storage filenames, atomic no-clobber initial persistence with bounded collision errors, and restart/Mermaid/concurrency regressions preserving original files

title: Model collaboration participants, processes, ownership, and flow scope correctly
description:
## What
Collaboration mutations collapse into one process: participants can serialize as tasks, requested pool size is discarded, nodes have no owner scope, and cross-pool flows cannot be classified. Build collaboration ownership before pool, lane, message-flow, or collaboration layout work.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a collaboration and add a pool with explicit size.
2. Add nodes intended for two pools and connect them.
3. Export and inspect semantic ownership, tags, refs, and DI.

## Where
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts
- src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts
- src/core/DiagramContext.ts
- src/server/tools.ts and handlers.ts
- tests/fixtures/collaboration/

## Implementation
- Add collaboration/process collections, participant.processRef, and node owner/process scope.
- Serialize participants/message flows under collaboration and flow nodes/sequence flows under the owning process.
- Allow element creation to target a scope and reject ambiguous or incompatible ownership.
- Preserve participant position/size and set BPMNPlane to collaboration.
- Define black-box participant behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Adding a pool never emits bpmn:task.
- Two participants own distinct processes with internal sequence flows and one cross-participant message flow.
- Invalid cross-scope sequence flows fail before mutation.
- Ownership, processRef, bounds, and flows survive save/reopen/mutate.

## Verification
- Parse a two-pool fixture with bpmn-moddle and assert owner collections, refs, flow types, and BPMNPlane.
- Import output with bpmn-js or an equivalent renderer smoke test.
- Run npm run type-check and focused collaboration tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adding a pool never emits bpmn:task.
- Two participants own distinct processes with internal sequence flows and one cross-participant message flow.
- Invalid cross-scope sequence flows fail before mutation.
- Ownership, processRef, bounds, and flows survive save/reopen/mutate.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: distinct participant process ownership, scoped sequence/message flows, black-box pools, safe scope rejection, and save/reopen DI round-trips.

title: Replace flat string templates with a schema-aware BPMN document model and serializer
description:
## What
The live engine rebuilds diagrams from a flat element map and silently coerces unsupported BPMN types to tasks. Introduce one typed document model and exhaustive serializer so processes, collaborations, hierarchy, artifacts, references, and BPMN DI remain structurally valid after mutations.

## Where
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts
- src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts
- src/core/DiagramContext.ts
- src/types/index.ts
- src/server/handlers.ts
- tests/unit/core/ and tests/integration/

## Implementation
- Use bpmn-moddle for parse/create/serialize, or a typed intermediate model with exhaustive serializers and no fallback-to-task behavior.
- Represent definitions, processes, collaborations, participants, nested scopes, artifacts, connections, references, and DI separately.
- Replace Map<string, any> domain state with typed discriminated elements and connections carrying owner/scope IDs.
- Centralize XML text/attribute serialization and reference generation.
- Define migration behavior for diagrams already persisted by the string-template engine.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every BPMN type advertised by src/server/tools.ts either serializes to its correct moddle type or is explicitly rejected as unsupported.
- Unknown element/connection types fail without mutating state or files.
- Process and collaboration roots, IDs, refs, and BPMNPlane targets remain correct after add/update/delete/connect operations.
- Names and labels containing all XML metacharacters and Unicode round-trip unchanged.
- Existing supported basic process creation remains compatible.

## Verification
- Add table-driven fixtures for every advertised type and parse each export with bpmn-moddle.
- Round-trip parse -> serialize -> parse and compare semantic types, IDs, refs, and DI.
- Run npm run type-check and focused core/handler Jest suites.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every BPMN type advertised by src/server/tools.ts either serializes to its correct moddle type or is explicitly rejected as unsupported.
- Unknown element/connection types fail without mutating state or files.
- Process and collaboration roots, IDs, refs, and BPMNPlane targets remain correct after add/update/delete/connect operations.
- Names and labels containing all XML metacharacters and Unicode round-trip unchanged.
- Existing supported basic process creation remains compatible.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: canonical typed BPMN document model with exhaustive bpmn-moddle serialization, safe rejection, correct roots/refs/DI, and round-trip coverage for every advertised type.

title: Path traversal and symlink escape in open/delete file tools and latent FileManager containment bug
description:
## What
open_bpmn, open_mermaid_file, and delete_diagram_file join client input directly beneath the diagrams path and permit traversal/absolute/symlink escapes. save_as currently sanitizes separators, so it is not directly exploitable through filename, but FileManager.validatePath uses an unsafe prefix comparison and its directory-capable API remains a latent escape risk.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a temporary configured diagrams root and an outside sentinel file plus an in-root symlink to it.
2. Call each open/delete entry point with ../, absolute, sibling-prefix, Windows separator/drive/UNC, and symlink forms.
3. Observe outside read/delete access on vulnerable paths; separately verify save_as sanitization and the FileManager sibling-prefix defect.

## Where
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts loadDiagram() (~lines 374-378) and deleteDiagram() (~lines 383-386); src/server/handlers.ts openMermaidFile() (~lines 158-163) and openBpmn() (~lines 142-146); src/utils/FileManager.ts validatePath() (~lines 69-74) and saveBpmnFile() (~lines 79-137).

## Implementation
- Create one canonical path resolver used by every open/save/save_as/delete/Mermaid file operation.
- Define basename-only or documented relative-path policy; reject absolute paths and enforce extension allowlists.
- Use path.relative with separator-aware containment, never string startsWith.
- Use lstat/realpath policy to reject symlink escapes; for destructive operations document residual race behavior rather than assuming stat-then-unlink is race-free.
- Return bounded errors without exposing sensitive absolute paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No file tool can read, write, or delete outside the configured root through traversal, absolute, sibling-prefix, Windows, or symlink input.
- Valid in-root BPMN/Mermaid operations continue to work.
- Outside sentinels remain unread and unmodified; wrong extensions and empty/dot names reject before I/O.

## Verification
- Run temp-root table tests for POSIX and Windows path forms, sibling-prefix paths, symlinks, empty names, and extension policy.
- Run focused file security tests and npm run type-check.
acceptance_criteria:
- No file tool can read, write, or delete outside the configured root through traversal, absolute, sibling-prefix, Windows, or symlink input.
- Valid in-root BPMN/Mermaid operations continue to work.
- Outside sentinels remain unread and unmodified; wrong extensions and empty/dot names reject before I/O.
notes:
## Prerelease review residual race (2026-08-22)
The basename/extension/symlink checks fixed direct traversal, but the security claim remains incomplete: `resolveSafeFilePath` performs lstat/realpath and returns a pathname, then callers later use ordinary `fs.open`, `fs.rename`, or `fs.unlink`. A local attacker who can mutate the diagrams directory can exchange the checked leaf or parent between validation and use (TOCTOU), reaching a symlink/outside inode.

Where: src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts lines 41-97; src/utils/FileManager.ts lines 137-147 and 220-258; src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts lines 927-938.
Implementation: for reads use no-follow open where supported and compare post-open fstat identity/type to the validated object; for write/delete document and implement a descriptor-relative strategy (`openat`/`renameat`/`unlinkat` via a vetted native boundary) or constrain directory ownership/permissions as an explicit platform policy. Never claim stat-then-use is race-free.
Verification: a synchronized adversarial test swaps the leaf and parent after resolution but before open/rename/unlink; outside sentinels must remain unread/unmodified on each supported platform.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: pinned all BPMN/Mermaid file operations to one root identity with anchored no-follow read, atomic write, and safe delete handling plus synchronized traversal/symlink race regressions

title: Fix production dependency vulnerabilities (1 critical, several high, incl. in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk itself)
description:
## What
A dated npm audit reports 17 production findings (1 critical, 5 high, 11 moderate). Direct risks include the MCP SDK and uuid; mermaid is a direct dependency with no source import and brings a large vulnerable tree. Counts are snapshots and must be re-measured from package-lock.json.

## Where
- package.json and package-lock.json
- imports under src/ and tests/
- CI audit gate created by mcp-bpmn-aek

## Implementation
- Confirm and remove unused mermaid if build/tests need no runtime import.
- Upgrade @modelcontextprotocol/sdk to a non-vulnerable compatible release and run protocol compatibility tests.
- Upgrade/remove direct uuid; only required APIs should remain.
- Use npm audit fix --dry-run before any automated lock rewrite; apply reviewed upgrades explicitly.
- Add an audit gate or an accepted-risk record containing advisory, reachability, owner, justification, and expiry.
- Audit full dependencies as well as production because tooling vulnerabilities affect CI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high has no unaccepted high/critical findings.
- Every accepted finding has a durable owner and expiry.
- Clean install, build, type-check, focused tests, strict e2e, and package smoke tests pass.
- No unused direct dependency remains.

## Verification
- Run npm ci, npm audit --omit=dev --json, npm audit --json, and rg import inventory.
- Run build/type-check/focused tests/e2e and npm pack --dry-run.
acceptance_criteria:
- npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high has no unaccepted high/critical findings.
- Every accepted finding has a durable owner and expiry.
- Clean install, build, type-check, focused tests, strict e2e, and package smoke tests pass.
- No unused direct dependency remains.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: upgraded MCP SDK and uuid, removed unused direct dependencies, refreshed the audited lockfile, and added zero-finding production/full audit gates.

title: Security & Hardening
description:
## Scope
Prevent untrusted MCP inputs, files, XML, dependencies, and expensive operations from escaping configured boundaries or destabilizing the server.

## Success Criteria
- All P0/P1 security children are closed or carry a documented, owned, time-bounded risk acceptance.
- Every file operation enforces one canonical root, symlink policy, extension policy, and bounded I/O.
- All tool arguments are runtime-validated before state or filesystem mutation.
- Generated/imported XML is parser-valid and user text cannot inject markup.
- Production dependency scans have no unaccepted high/critical findings.

## Verification
- Run focused security suites, npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high, npm run type-check, and the final clean-check command.
acceptance_criteria:
All P0/P1 security children are closed or carry a documented, owned, time-bounded risk acceptance.
Every file operation enforces one canonical root, symlink policy, extension policy, and bounded I/O.
All tool arguments are runtime-validated before state or filesystem mutation.
Generated/imported XML is parser-valid and user text cannot inject markup.
Production dependency scans have no unaccepted high/critical findings.

title: tools/list is 134 KB, roughly 34,000 tokens an agent pays before its first call
description:
## Evidence

Measured from a live tools/list against the built server (41 tools, 137,551 bytes in the tools array; token figures are bytes/4, so approximate).

Where the bytes go:

    outputSchema   75,008  (54%)
    inputSchema    47,268  (34%)
    descriptions    8,078  ( 5%)   <- the part a model actually reads to choose a tool
    annotations     3,679  ( 2%)

The tool descriptions, which are what the model needs, are 5% of what it is charged for.

## Ranked levers, each measured

1. outputSchema is the whole problem. Removing it entirely: 137,551 -> 61,845 bytes, -55%. It is optional in MCP, and its only job is letting a client validate structuredContent.
2. description strings *inside* outputSchema: 18,768 bytes. These are read by no one — the model does not see output schemas in most hosts, and a validator ignores them. Free to delete.
3. The tool-error branch added for mcp-bpmn-8u0.11 is 325 bytes duplicated across all 41 tools = 13,325 bytes. A minimal {code, message, additionalProperties:true} branch is about a quarter of that.
4. Within-schema $ref/$defs: -16,780 bytes (12%). Note the limit: each tool's inputSchema and outputSchema is a standalone JSON Schema document in MCP, so a $ref cannot reach a definition in another tool. Cross-tool sharing would save 42% but the protocol has no place to put it.
5. The repeats that drive 4: the BPMN id string (114 occurrences, 84 bytes each), the revision token (53 x 146), position/size (25 x 196), the geometry diagnostic (11 x ~300).

Combining 2, 3 and 4 without removing outputSchema: 137,551 -> 107,084 bytes, -22%, about 26,800 tokens.
Doing that and dropping outputSchema where it earns nothing gets under 15,000.

## Impact

Every session pays this before the agent can do anything, on every host that lists tools eagerly. It is a fixed tax on a 41-tool server, and it grows with each tool added.

## Fix

Take 2 and 3 first: they are pure deletion with no contract change. Then decide 1 deliberately — keep outputSchema on the query tools whose shape a client benefits from validating, drop it where the result is a short mutation ack. Add a test that fails when the serialized tools/list crosses a byte budget, the way the existing size guard does, so this cannot drift back.
close_reason: tools/list went from 137,551 to 117,183 bytes, roughly 34,400 to 29,300 tokens, a 15% cut delivered while the surface also grew by five new fields. Three changes: every description was stripped from output schemas (a validator ignores prose and hosts do not show output schemas to the model), the duplicated error branch lost its two descriptions, and repeated output sub-schemas are now shared through $ref. The $ref work needed care: the generator emits pointers relative to its own document root, and wrapping that document as anyOf[0] moved it, so rebaseRefs re-points them or they would resolve to nothing and silently accept anything. Pinned by three tests: a 120,000-byte budget, an assertion that no output schema carries prose, and one that compiles every schema with Ajv and proves a referenced constraint still rejects a bad value. Did not remove outputSchema wholesale, which would have saved 55% but cost the e2e suite its per-tool validation.

title: No way to set isForCompensation, so a compensation handler cannot be authored correctly
description:
## Evidence

Found by driving the built server over stdio as an agent.

add_activity rejects it:

    {"code":"invalid_arguments","message":"properties: Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'isForCompensation'"}

The supported activity properties are isExpanded, calledElement, assignee, candidateGroups, dueDate and multiInstance. grep -rn isForCompensation src/ returns nothing: the attribute is not read on import, not written on export, and not settable.

The exported handler is therefore:

    <bpmn:task id="Task_3" name="Release stock" />

with no isForCompensation="true".

## Impact

The server can create a compensation boundary event and associate it with a handler, but the handler is not marked as a compensation handler, so the exported XML does not express the pattern. A downstream engine reads it as an unreachable orphan task. The compensation feature is advertised but cannot produce a correct model, and the missing attribute is also what would let the validator stop reporting mcp-bpmn-a3j.30.

## Fix

Accept isForCompensation on add_activity and update_element properties, capture it on import, write it on export, and pin a compensation round trip.
close_reason: isForCompensation is accepted on add_activity and update_element, written by BpmnDocument on serialize and read back on import, and rejected on an element type that is not an activity. Pinned by 'marks a compensation handler and an event subprocess, and round-trips both', which asserts the attribute reaches the XML and survives save, close and reopen.

title: Validator reports three false positives against a correct compensation model
description:
## Evidence

Found by driving the built server over stdio as an agent, modelling a compensation pattern: a compensation boundary event on "Reserve stock", associated with a "Release stock" handler.

validate level full on the finished, structurally valid diagram:

    warning BPMN_PROFILE_MISSING_INCOMING_FLOW  Task_3          Flow node should have an incoming sequence flow
    warning BPMN_PROFILE_MISSING_OUTGOING_FLOW  BoundaryEvent_2 Flow node should have an outgoing sequence flow
    warning BPMN_PROFILE_MISSING_OUTGOING_FLOW  Task_3          Flow node should have an outgoing sequence flow

All three are wrong. In BPMN a compensation boundary event is connected to its handler by an Association, never by a sequence flow, and the handler sits outside the normal flow with no incoming or outgoing sequence flow. The diagram is correct as modelled.

## Impact

An agent that follows this guidance will wire sequence flows into a compensation handler and produce invalid BPMN. This is the same false-positive class that mcp-bpmn-a3j.19 and the subprocess and lane rules had, now on the compensation pattern, which the tool surface advertises through the compensation event definition.

## Fix

Exempt from the incoming and outgoing flow rules: any activity that is a compensation handler (the target of an Association whose source is a compensation boundary event, or an activity with isForCompensation true once mcp-bpmn-9sv.18 makes that settable), and any compensation boundary event. Add a no-false-positive twin asserting the model above validates clean.
close_reason: BpmnValidator now exempts compensation handlers and compensation boundary events from the executable-profile incoming/outgoing sequence flow warnings. A handler is detected structurally (target of an Association whose source is a boundary event carrying bpmn:CompensateEventDefinition) via the new collectCompensationHandlers/isCompensationBoundaryEvent helpers, and isForCompensation=true is honoured wherever a document already carries it, so the rule keeps working once mcp-bpmn-9sv.18 lands. Pinned by 'does not ask a compensation handler or its boundary event for sequence flows' and 'exempts a handler marked isForCompensation even with no association' in tests/unit/core/BpmnValidator.test.ts (both fail before, pass after); no-false-positive twins 'still asks a task associated with a non-compensation boundary event for its flows' and 'still asks a disconnected task alongside a compensation handler for its flows' prove the exemption is not over-broad.

title: build_process cannot create timer, error, signal or escalation events: it demands eventDefinitionPayload and rejects it as an unknown key
description:
## Evidence

Found by driving the built server over stdio as an agent.

Step 1 — a timer boundary event through build_process:

    {"kind":"event","ref":"timeout","eventType":"boundary","eventDefinition":"timer","attachTo":"UserTask_1",...}

rejected with:

    {"code":"unexpected_error","message":"nodes[0] (ref \"timeout\"): Timer event definition requires eventDefinitionPayload.timer with type and a non-empty expression"}

Step 2 — adding the field the error names:

    {"code":"invalid_arguments","message":"nodes.0: Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'eventDefinitionPayload'"}

## Cause

add_event declares eventDefinitionPayload; the buildNode schema in src/server/tools.ts does not, and the node object is .strict(). The engine still runs the same validation, so every event definition that needs a payload is unreachable through build_process: timer always, and error/signal/escalation wherever a reference is required.

## Impact

build_process is the tool that makes a multi-element process one atomic call. Any realistic process with a timer boundary event has to fall back to per-element add_event calls, which is the round-trip cost the tool exists to remove. The two errors also contradict each other, so an agent cannot recover by reading them.

## Fix

Add eventDefinitionPayload to the event branch of buildNode with the same schema add_event uses, and classify the engine's message as invalid_arguments (or invalid_bpmn) with a recovery hint rather than unexpected_error.

The engine message that demanded it is classified invalid_arguments with a recovery hint instead of unexpected_error. build_process also resolves a ref in attachTo the way it resolves flow endpoints, so a boundary event and its host can be created in one call. Pinned by 'creates a timer boundary event through build_process' in tests/integration/handlers.test.ts, which asserts bpmn:timeDuration and P14D reach the XML.

title: Router and oracle ignore collinear/parallel edge overlap; message flows dock on sequence-flow endpoints
description:
## Evidence
After auto_layout of a 2-pool collaboration: `MessageFlow_2 (586,530)->(736,530)->(736,200)` lies on `Flow_7 (586,530)->(736,530)->…` for 150px; `MessageFlow_3` ends `(1006,160)->(986,160)` on `Flow_4 (986,160)->…` (arrowhead on the sequence-flow exit point); in a 2-pool probe the message flow starts on the incoming sequence flow's arrowhead. The oracle reports `0px apart` but the router reports zero diagnostics because segmentsProperlyCross ignores parallel segments and the score has no proximity term (src/core/layout/ConnectionRouter.ts:330-334, :549-568, :426-452; src/core/layout/CollaborationLayoutPolicy.ts:324-348).

## Fix
Add a parallel-segment proximity/collinear check in inspectRoute; treat a shared dock point as a collision; dock message flows on the top/bottom of shapes, sequence flows on left/right.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. The oracle now resolves container ancestry by walking parentId, so shapes and labels never collide with their own pool, lane or expanded subprocess; bpmn:DataObject is registered non-visual; collinear/parallel edge overlap is reported and a shared dock is only excused between connectors of the same type. The router excludes scope ancestors from obstacles (so flows inside a subprocess route), treats a foreign participant as a hard obstacle for sequence flows, and steers message flows onto top/bottom docks. Pools are aligned to one left edge and width, and a pool size the caller never requested is no longer treated as a layout floor (size provenance is tracked through createElement). 3g8.4: the DI shape/edge arrays are hoisted out of the message-flow routing loop. 3g8.5, 5e7.4 and 5e7.5 were already implemented at HEAD; coverage was extended and the collinear blind spot in EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING closed.

title: apply_geometry_patch optimistic-concurrency rejections and snap-to-boundary are untested
description:
## Evidence
Uncovered src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:1436-1441 and :1447-1452 (ConnectionGeometryConflictError throws inside applyGeometryPatch) and :1475-1486 (snap-to-boundary in the same method). Existing waypoints_mismatch / geometry_revision_mismatch assertions (tests/integration/handlers.test.ts:1506-1520, :2554-2565) target update_connection_geometry / route_connection only. GeometryPatchConflictError is never constructed in tests.

## Impact
A stale connection patch could be silently applied, clobbering another editor's change; batch rollback on connection conflict is unverified.

## Fix
Add stale-revision, stale-waypoints, mixed-batch atomicity, labelBounds-conflict, and snap-to-boundary cases through apply_geometry_patch.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 5e7.6: a table-driven case per validator rule, each pairing a violation fixture (asserting the code and the exact element it names) with a legal twin that must validate clean, plus a coverage floor for BpmnValidator.ts; BPMN_INVALID_DEFINITIONS is documented as unreachable through the public API and pinned through the parser seam. 5e7.7: new geometry-concurrency suite covers stale revisions, stale waypoints, mixed-batch rollback, labelBounds conflicts and snap-to-boundary, each asserting memory, revision and disk are unchanged. 5e7.10: a single-field-mutation table over three clean baselines covers every validateLayoutModel code, with a meta-test that scrapes the source so a new code fails until covered. 5e7.11: e2e now pins unknown methods, malformed JSON-RPC, unknown tools and wrong-typed arguments, plus the error-code taxonomy. 5e7.12: fixtures exported by Camunda Modeler 7 and 8, bpmn-js and Eclipse BPMN2 Modeler, asserted for id, namespace and DI survival across open/edit/reopen/export. 5e7.8: e2e forwards PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR wherever HOME is isolated. 5e7.9: test:all runs with coverage so the thresholds are enforced by the gate.

title: Mermaid: cross-subgraph edges with gateway/event endpoints fail late with BPMN IDs, or produce spec-invalid message flows
description:
## Evidence
Pools a (S((Start)) -> T -> G{Which?}) and b (U -> E((End))) plus root `G --> U`: parser passes (src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:545-554); generator emits messageFlow Gateway_G->Task_U (src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts:175-191); on the default layout path documentSerializer.parse throws `Imported message flow MessageFlow_6 is invalid: Message flow endpoint Gateway_G is not a BPMN interaction node` (BPMN ids the agent never saw, no line/column). With autoLayout=false the invalid XML is returned. Also `S --> U` (start event as message-flow source) and `T --> E` (end event as target) are accepted end-to-end though BPMN forbids both; INTERACTION_NODE_TYPES (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:84-93) includes them and BpmnValidator.ts:377-402 does not check.

## Impact
The documented collaboration bootstrap workflow (skills/bpmn-modeler/references/workflows.md:32-42) hits an opaque late failure, and silently produces spec-invalid message flows.

## Fix
In validateAST, for edges whose endpoints have different owners, emit UNSUPPORTED_EDGE_ENDPOINT with line/column when either endpoint is a decision node, the source is a start node, or the target is an end node. Add the start/end rule to resolveMessageFlowParticipant / BpmnValidator.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. j21.1: a start/end label is dropped only when the normalized label is exactly a keyword, so 'Order Started' and 'Send Invoice' keep their names and the process name is no longer built by string replacement. j21.2: cross-subgraph edges with a gateway endpoint, a start-event source or an end-event target now fail at parse time with UNSUPPORTED_EDGE_ENDPOINT carrying line, column and the author's Mermaid ids, instead of failing later against generated BPMN ids; the validator half was added separately as BPMN_INVALID_MESSAGE_FLOW_DIRECTION. j21.3: semicolon statement terminators and 'graph TD;' headers parse, with splitting suppressed inside brackets, quotes, edge labels, entities and comments.

title: Mermaid: semicolon statement terminators and 'graph TD;' headers are rejected
description:
## Evidence
`graph TD; A-->B;` -> `1:7 [MALFORMED_HEADER]` (column points at the valid TD). `A[Start] --> B[Work];` -> `2:23 [MALFORMED_EDGE] Unexpected content after the target node` on every line. src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:59, :109-122, :322-329. Semicolons are the canonical separator in Mermaid's own docs and in most LLM-emitted Mermaid; neither skills/bpmn-modeler/references/capabilities.md:59-72 nor README.md:213-232 say they are unsupported.

## Impact
A large share of realistic agent input is rejected outright.

## Fix
Strip trailing `;` and split statements on `;` outside []{}()""||; accept `^(graph|flowchart)\s+(TD|TB|LR|RL|BT)\s*;?` and treat the remainder of the line as the next statement.

title: npm run audit:prod fails: high-severity fast-uri (and moderate qs) via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
description:
## Evidence
`npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` exits 1: fast-uri 3.0.0-3.1.5 high (GHSA-5jgf-p345-68v8, GHSA-f65p-4m7j-42xc, GHSA-fph4-wmhf-6fwf, GHSA-jqff-g426-hqxp) plus qs moderate. `npm ls` shows both come from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.26.0 (ajv@8.20.0 -> fast-uri@3.1.5; express@5.2.1 -> qs@6.15.3). npm reports a fix available via `npm audit fix`.

## Impact
`npm run check` is red; CONTRIBUTING says do not bypass the audit; a release would ship a known high advisory in its production tree.

## Fix
`npm audit fix` or an `overrides` entry for fast-uri, regenerate both lockfiles (they must stay identical), or bump the SDK; re-run audit:prod and update the packed-contract fingerprint if tools/list changes.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 8u0.10: new build_process tool creates many elements and their flows in one transaction, addressed by caller-chosen refs; the engine gained a batch mode so nested mutations join one lock, one serialization and one write, and a failure anywhere leaves the diagram untouched. 8u0.11: every failed call returns {code, message, recovery, ...context}; the advertised output schemas accept that shape, without which MCP clients reject error responses with -32602 once they have listed tools (this also fixed the pre-existing conflict errors). 3g8.12: pools stack below existing participants instead of all defaulting to (100,100). 33g.12: fast-uri and qs overridden to patched versions, both lockfiles regenerated and identical, npm audit clean.

title: Decide the release version and bring CHANGELOG up to date (five commits and 12 of 39 tools undocumented)
description:
## Evidence
No git tags. CHANGELOG.md:8-12 says "No version has been assigned" and :87-92 says it "does not invent a 0.2.0 release", while package.json:3, .codex-plugin/plugin.json:3 and .claude-plugin/plugin.json:3 all say 0.2.0. Unreleased traces only to eab3fb6; commits cc5a2ab, 3a1c4dd, 7de9175, bf470cc, bb8fc1b (installer, Makefile, bin shim, plugin manifests, WorkspaceSession/.mcp-bpmn.json, get_workspace/select_workspace, save_svg/save_png, route_connection, apply_geometry_patch, update_*_geometry, analyze_geometry, list_connections/get_connection/update_connection) are undocumented. CHANGELOG.md:34-37 names only add_data_object, add_text_annotation, add_association; 12 shipped tools are unmentioned.

## Impact
No answer to "what version is this" and no release notes for most of the user-visible surface.

Maintainer picks the version (the list_elements/add_lane compatibility breaks justify at least a minor bump), moves Unreleased into a dated section covering every added tool and the update_connection revision requirement, and tags before npm pack.

title: Mermaid: node labels merely containing 'start'/'end' silently lose their names (Send Invoice, Vendor, Pending…)
description:
## Evidence
`A((Order Started)) --> B[Pack] --> C((Send Invoice))` -> `<bpmn:startEvent id="StartEvent_A" />` and `<bpmn:endEvent id="EndEvent_C" />` with no name, process name "Order ed". `A((Start Order)) … C((Order Ended))` -> both unnamed, process "Order". src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts:304-312 elementName() uses substring regexes /start/i and /end/i; src/converters/MermaidConverter.ts:276-282 generateProcessName does label.replace(/start|begin/gi,''). The parser (MermaidParser.ts:490-500) correctly uses exact keywords. No warning is emitted.

## Impact
Silent name loss on very common labels (Send…, Vendor…, Pending…, Restart…, Ended…).

## Fix
Drop the name only when the normalized label is exactly start|begin / end|stop|finish; use the start label verbatim (or "Converted Process") for the process name, never replace().

title: analyze_geometry false positives: labels and lane-parented shapes flagged against their own pool/lane/subprocess ancestors
description:
## Evidence
Two-pool collaboration with named events -> auto_layout OK -> analyze_geometry {} returns valid:false, summary {"total":4,"errors":4,"byCode":{"LABEL_OVERLAP":4}}, e.g. `Label StartEvent_1_label for StartEvent_1 overlaps shape Participant_1` (also `overlaps shape Lane_1`). The loop at src/core/BpmnGeometry.ts:810-819 tests every label against every shape on the plane, skipping only label.ownerId === shape.id; SHAPE_OVERLAP does not fire for the same containment, so the oracle is inconsistent with itself. The same process-only diagram after layout: valid:true.

## Impact
For any collaboration the geometry-valid signal is permanently false after the server's own layout, and update_element_geometry / apply_geometry_patch share the oracle with the default reject-new policy. Distinct from mcp-bpmn-5e7.5 (label-vs-label).

## Fix
Skip ancestor shapes (participant, lane, expanded subprocess containing the label owner) in the label loop, mirroring the containment logic used for shapes. Regression test: two-pool layout => analyze_geometry valid:true.
notes: Layout review confirmed the same root cause for SHAPE_OVERLAP: a clean laid-out 2-pool/2-lane collaboration returns valid:false with 6x SHAPE_OVERLAP ('Participant_2 overlaps SendTask_1' = lane-parented node vs pool grandparent, BpmnGeometry.ts:1023-1030, :762-785) plus 6x LABEL_OVERLAP. Laid-out tests/fixtures/import-roundtrip/full-semantics-di.bpmn yields 12 SHAPE_OVERLAP + 16 LABEL_OVERLAP, all of this kind. Fix both: treat ancestor/descendant pairs as legal by walking parentId (like isEndpointAncestor) and skip container ancestors in label-vs-shape.

The oracle now resolves container ancestry by walking parentId, so shapes and labels never collide with their own pool, lane or expanded subprocess; bpmn:DataObject is registered non-visual; collinear/parallel edge overlap is reported and a shared dock is only excused between connectors of the same type. The router excludes scope ancestors from obstacles (so flows inside a subprocess route), treats a foreign participant as a hard obstacle for sequence flows, and steers message flows onto top/bottom docks. Pools are aligned to one left edge and width, and a pool size the caller never requested is no longer treated as a layout floor (size provenance is tracked through createElement). 3g8.4: the DI shape/edge arrays are hoisted out of the message-flow routing loop. 3g8.5, 5e7.4 and 5e7.5 were already implemented at HEAD; coverage was extended and the collinear blind spot in EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING closed.

title: new_bpmn / new_from_mermaid cannot take a filename; the documented save_as path leaves an orphan base64-named duplicate
description:
## Evidence
new_bpmn returns filename `mcp-bpmn-v1_WyJQcm9jZXNzXzEiLCJBcHByb3ZhbCBQcm9jZXNzIiwi….bpmn` (95 chars; src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2822-2834 defaultFilename). After the README-documented `save_as {filename:"approval.bpmn"}` (README.md:865, :897; Examples 1-3 all do new_bpmn -> save_as), list_diagrams shows two entries with identical processId/name. new_bpmn/new_from_mermaid/open_mermaid_file (src/server/tools.ts:904-947) have no filename parameter.

## Impact
Every documented happy path litters the workspace with an opaque duplicate; agents cannot tell which file is canonical; the 95-char filename is echoed in every mutation result; delete_diagram_file needs user confirmation per server instructions so agents cannot clean up.

## Fix
Optional `filename` on new_bpmn/new_from_mermaid/open_mermaid_file; make save_as remove the untouched auto-generated original (or return previousFilename); use a readable default `<sanitized-name>.bpmn` with a numeric suffix on collision. Update README accordingly.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 8u0.1: the expanded XML NCName character class is validated by a refinement instead of an advertised pattern, taking tools/list from 168 KB to 129 KB; a contract test bounds the size and proves NCName is still enforced. 8u0.2: new_bpmn/new_from_mermaid/open_mermaid_file accept a filename, and save_as removes a server-generated placeholder while never removing a caller-chosen name. 8u0.3: delete_element reports removedElementIds/removedElementCount and the description states container cascade. 8u0.4: elementType is an enum of every listable BPMN type. 8u0.5: get_element points at get_connection for connection ids and names the rendered reference for a backing DataObject.

title: tools/list is 168 KB; one NCName regex is repeated 149 times (37% of the bytes)
description:
## Evidence
JSON.stringify(tools) from the live server = 168,377 bytes for 39 tools. The 415-byte escaped BPMN_ID_PATTERN (src/utils/BpmnId.ts:8-11, emitted via bpmnId()/outputBpmnId in src/server/tools.ts:307-310, :395-398) appears 149 times = 61,835 bytes. Output schemas alone are ~100 KB. Largest tools: update_connection 14.5 KB, apply_geometry_patch 14.2 KB, analyze_geometry 11.5 KB, route_connection 9.7 KB, get_element 9.0 KB.

## Impact
Roughly 40k+ tokens of tool definitions before an agent does anything; some hosts truncate or refuse large tool lists; every session pays this cost.

## Fix
Drop `pattern` from the JSON output of bpmnId()/outputBpmnId (keep runtime validation; or use a short pattern like `^[A-Za-z_][\w.\-]*$`), consider `$refStrategy:'root'` so shared definitions are emitted once, and trim output schemas for the geometry tools. Add a test pinning an upper bound on tools/list size.

title: Camunda 7 calledElement expressions are rejected on import and reported as 'malformed or invalid input'
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:2213-2215 readFlowNode throws when calledElement is not a QName. Camunda 7 models routinely use `calledElement="${notifyProcess}"` (documented feature written by Camunda Modeler). Raw error: `Call activity CallActivity_1 calledElement must be a valid BPMN QName`; through importXml (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2994-3020 safeImportError) the agent sees only `Failed to parse BPMN XML: malformed or invalid input`. With a plain name the same file imports fine as camunda7.

## Impact
Any Camunda 7 model with an expression-bound call activity cannot be opened, and the agent is told the file is malformed. These are exactly the files the camunda7 profile (ADR 0001) targets.

## Fix
Treat calledElement as opaque on import (enforce QName only for API-authored values in the portable profile); at minimum let the message through safeImportError.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. a3j.10: indexFlowContainer no longer overwrites the parent-scope entry it just recorded for a subprocess; lanes are also indexed so a lane-endpoint association resolves. A fixture-corpus test pins validator output for every shipped fixture. a3j.11: reconcileRetainedDiagram drops DI whose bpmnElement is no longer reachable from the definitions tree, so nested data associations take their edges with them. a3j.12: deleteElement clears compensation activityRef and multi-instance loopData refs that point at deleted elements. a3j.13: calledElement is opaque on import and validated only when authored, with Camunda expressions accepted under the camunda7 profile.

title: SVG/PNG rendering fails when the server runs as root; no way to pass Chrome launch args
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnSvgRenderer.ts:397-421 launchBrowser() never sets `args` and honours no env override besides PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH. With Puppeteer's managed Chrome present, export {format:"svg"}, save_svg, save_png all return: `Error: SVG export requires Chrome or Chromium. Install Puppeteer's managed browser or set PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH … Browser launch failed: … Running as root without --no-sandbox is not supported.` The renderer test suite fails 3/3 as root and the e2e SVG test fails identically; a wrapper adding --no-sandbox makes all of them pass. Docs (README.md:35-46, docs/agent-client-troubleshooting.md:120-135) never mention the sandbox.

## Impact
Agent runtimes (Docker, devcontainers, CI, cloud sandboxes) commonly run as root; the whole visual-output family is dead there and the error points at the wrong remedy. Contributors in such environments cannot run npm test. Also the root cause behind the permanently red CI (see CI bead).

## Fix
Add MCP_BPMN_BROWSER_ARGS (or add `--no-sandbox --disable-setuid-sandbox` automatically when process.getuid?.()===0), mention it in the launch error and the troubleshooting doc, and have tests set it when uid is 0.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. BpmnSvgRenderer honours MCP_BPMN_BROWSER_ARGS and adds --no-sandbox --disable-setuid-sandbox when running as uid 0; the launch error names the sandbox cause. Renderer suite went 3/3 failing to 6/6 passing as root.

title: validate falsely reports BPMN_CROSS_SCOPE_SEQUENCE_FLOW for every flow into/out of a subprocess (and lanes referencing one)
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnValidator.ts indexFlowContainer registers a subprocess as a flow node of its parent (line 276, scopeId = parent), then recurses (line 282, scopeId = item.id) whose first statement (line 273) `semanticById.set(container.id, …)` overwrites the entry with scopeId === item.id. Reproduced via MCP: new_bpmn -> start -> add_activity subProcess -> end -> connect x2 -> validate semantic => `valid:false`, BPMN_CROSS_SCOPE_SEQUENCE_FLOW on both flows. The repo's own fixtures fail the same way when opened and validated: tests/fixtures/layout/subprocess-boundary.bpmn (Flow_Outer_1/2), engine-contract/hierarchy-extensions-labels-di.bpmn, import-roundtrip/full-semantics-di.bpmn (plus BPMN_INVALID_LANE_REFERENCE:Lane_Reviewer and BPMN_ASSOCIATION_OUTSIDE_OWNER). `grep -rn CROSS_SCOPE tests` finds no test; both subprocess sites in tests/integration/handlers.test.ts (1360, 2112) never call validate.

## Impact
validate at semantic/full returns valid:false for every diagram containing a connected subprocess or a lane containing a subprocess, including the engine's own output. Agents "fix" valid models or loop; the skill runs validate before export.

## Fix
In indexFlowContainer do not overwrite an existing semanticById entry for the container (`if (!semanticById.has(container.id))`), registering root processes separately. Add: validator unit case Start->SubProcess->End => zero errors; handler test authoring a subprocess => valid:true; a fixture-corpus test pinning validate output per fixture file.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. a3j.10: indexFlowContainer no longer overwrites the parent-scope entry it just recorded for a subprocess; lanes are also indexed so a lane-endpoint association resolves. A fixture-corpus test pins validator output for every shipped fixture. a3j.11: reconcileRetainedDiagram drops DI whose bpmnElement is no longer reachable from the definitions tree, so nested data associations take their edges with them. a3j.12: deleteElement clears compensation activityRef and multi-instance loopData refs that point at deleted elements. a3j.13: calledElement is opaque on import and validated only when authored, with Camunda expressions accepted under the camunda7 profile.

title: delete_element fails for activities carrying data input/output associations (DI edges never detached)
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:1105-1142 detachSemantic(task) clears only references whose value is the task and the task's own containment. Nested bpmn:dataInputAssociation / dataOutputAssociation children vanish with it, but the plane's BPMNEdges referencing them are neither detached nor filtered by reconcileRetainedDiagram (filter at :1511 only drops edges for SequenceFlow|MessageFlow|Association). The post-serialization re-parse then rejects the document. On a Camunda-Modeler-style file: `delete Task_Review FAILED: Retained BPMN mutation produced invalid references: DataInputAssociation_1, DataOutputAssociation_1`.

## Impact
Deleting any task that uses a data object/store the way Camunda Modeler and bpmn.io express it is impossible on imported files; the tool returns an opaque error and rolls back.

## Fix
In detachSemantic walk the containment tree of the detached semantic and remove plane elements whose bpmnElement is any descendant with an id; or after all detaches drop every BPMNShape/BPMNEdge whose bpmnElement is no longer reachable from definitions. Add an import + delete regression test with data associations.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. a3j.10: indexFlowContainer no longer overwrites the parent-scope entry it just recorded for a subprocess; lanes are also indexed so a lane-endpoint association resolves. A fixture-corpus test pins validator output for every shipped fixture. a3j.11: reconcileRetainedDiagram drops DI whose bpmnElement is no longer reachable from the definitions tree, so nested data associations take their edges with them. a3j.12: deleteElement clears compensation activityRef and multi-instance loopData refs that point at deleted elements. a3j.13: calledElement is opaque on import and validated only when authored, with Camunda expressions accepted under the camunda7 profile.

title: Deleting an element referenced by a compensation activityRef or multi-instance loopData*Ref fails with an opaque error
description:
## Evidence
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:1788-1793 deleteElement never touches eventDefinitionPayload.activityRef on compensation events or multiInstance.loopDataInputRef/loopDataOutputRef on other activities. On serialization applyEventDefinitionProperties (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:1332-1337, :1990-2001) re-resolves payload.activityRef from semanticById (which still holds the detached object) and verification fails: `compensation delete FAILED: Retained BPMN mutation produced invalid references: Task_1` (task still present afterwards); `MI delete FAILED: … invalid references: DataObjectReference_1`.

## Impact
An agent that created a compensation throw event with activityRef, or a multi-instance activity bound to a data object reference, can never delete the referenced element, and the error does not name the referrer.

## Fix
In deleteElement null out activityRef / delete loopData*Ref on surviving elements when they point into idsToDelete (or reject with a message naming the referrer); resolve those ids against document.elements rather than the stale semanticById.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. a3j.10: indexFlowContainer no longer overwrites the parent-scope entry it just recorded for a subprocess; lanes are also indexed so a lane-endpoint association resolves. A fixture-corpus test pins validator output for every shipped fixture. a3j.11: reconcileRetainedDiagram drops DI whose bpmnElement is no longer reachable from the definitions tree, so nested data associations take their edges with them. a3j.12: deleteElement clears compensation activityRef and multi-instance loopData refs that point at deleted elements. a3j.13: calledElement is opaque on import and validated only when authored, with Camunda expressions accepted under the camunda7 profile.

title: Agent Experience — tool ergonomics, error design, and response cost
description:
## Scope
Make the MCP tool surface pleasant for AI agents: self-describing schemas, actionable errors with recovery hints, minimal round trips for common edits, and responses that do not waste tokens. Findings come from driving the built server over stdio through realistic agent flows (approval process, two-pool collaboration, geometry edits, error paths).

## Success Criteria
- Every error names the offending ID/parameter and the next action.
- Common edits (rename a flow, fix an annotation, build a small process) need one call, not two or more.
- tools/list and per-call payloads are compact; no duplicated JSON in text + structuredContent.
- README, skill, and tool descriptions agree with real behavior.

title: LABEL_OVERLAP diagnostic checks label vs shape only — label-label overlaps are invisible to the oracle
description: validateShapeAndLabelOverlaps() in tests/helpers/bpmnGeometry.ts compares each label against every shape (node/container), but never compares labels against other labels. Two edge labels — e.g. from adjacent sequence flows or multiple message flows between the same participant pair — can overlap each other without triggering any LABEL_OVERLAP diagnostic. The layout-candidate test matrix therefore cannot surface label-label collisions, leaving a blind spot in the quality gate used to validate the chosen layout library.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. The oracle now resolves container ancestry by walking parentId, so shapes and labels never collide with their own pool, lane or expanded subprocess; bpmn:DataObject is registered non-visual; collinear/parallel edge overlap is reported and a shared dock is only excused between connectors of the same type. The router excludes scope ancestors from obstacles (so flows inside a subprocess route), treats a foreign participant as a hard obstacle for sequence flows, and steers message flows onto top/bottom docks. Pools are aligned to one left edge and width, and a pool size the caller never requested is no longer treated as a layout floor (size provenance is tracked through createElement). 3g8.4: the DI shape/edge arrays are hoisted out of the message-flow routing loop. 3g8.5, 5e7.4 and 5e7.5 were already implemented at HEAD; coverage was extended and the collinear blind spot in EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING closed.

title: Geometry oracle missing EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING check — connector criss-crossing goes undetected
description: The fixture geometry validator (tests/helpers/bpmnGeometry.ts) checks SHAPE_OVERLAP, LABEL_OVERLAP (label vs shape), EDGE_SHAPE_COLLISION, and CONTAINMENT_FAILURE, but has no EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING diagnostic. Two connectors can cross each other without triggering any validation failure, so the layout-candidate test matrix reports 'valid geometry' for diagrams that still have criss-crossing edges. This makes it impossible to know whether the chosen layout library (bpmn-auto-layout@2.0.0-alpha.2) actually eliminates edge crossings across the fixture corpus, which is the primary goal of the layout epic.

The oracle now resolves container ancestry by walking parentId, so shapes and labels never collide with their own pool, lane or expanded subprocess; bpmn:DataObject is registered non-visual; collinear/parallel edge overlap is reported and a shared dock is only excused between connectors of the same type. The router excludes scope ancestors from obstacles (so flows inside a subprocess route), treats a foreign participant as a hard obstacle for sequence flows, and steers message flows onto top/bottom docks. Pools are aligned to one left edge and width, and a pool size the caller never requested is no longer treated as a layout floor (size provenance is tracked through createElement). 3g8.4: the DI shape/edge arrays are hoisted out of the message-flow routing loop. 3g8.5, 5e7.4 and 5e7.5 were already implemented at HEAD; coverage was extended and the collinear blind spot in EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING closed.

title: Make auto_layout honest about unsupported vertical layout
description:
## What / impact
The public MCP schema advertises `auto_layout.algorithm` values `horizontal` and `vertical`, but the engine unconditionally throws for vertical. A client can send schema-valid input that always fails as unimplemented, violating the central tool-contract promise and blocking generated clients from knowing supported behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create any current process through the handler.
2. Call auto_layout with algorithm=vertical, which tools/list declares valid.
3. Observe isError:true with the implementation-only-horizontal message.

## Evidence
`handleRequest('auto_layout',{algorithm:'vertical'})` returned `isError:true` with “Only horizontal layout algorithm is currently supported.” The contract suite acknowledges this as a TODO rather than an executable test.

## Where
- src/server/tools.ts:621-629
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:956-963
- src/core/layout/LayoutModel.ts and adapters
- tests/contracts/engine-contract.test.ts:442
- README auto-layout documentation

## Implementation direction
Choose one release scope. Preferred if vertical is required: map it to top-to-bottom layout through the canonical model/adapter and preserve collaboration/lane/waypoint invariants. Otherwise remove vertical from Zod/JSON Schema/TypeScript/docs now and add it back only with tests. Do not keep a knowingly dead enum branch.

## Verification
Assert tools/list schema parity with actual calls. For implementation, run horizontal and vertical golden geometry fixtures including disconnected nodes, cycles, subprocesses, pools/lanes, and message flows; prove dominant direction and no overlaps. For removal, assert vertical rejects at request validation as an unknown value and no docs/types advertise it.
acceptance_criteria: Every algorithm advertised by tools/list succeeds for supported fixture classes and reports its actual direction, or vertical is removed from runtime schema/types/docs until implemented; no valid advertised enum value deterministically returns an implementation error; contract/e2e tests cover the chosen behavior.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: removed unsupported vertical auto-layout from runtime schema/types/docs, deleted the dead engine branch, and added contract/e2e parity coverage for horizontal success and vertical validation rejection

title: Resolve bpmn-js watermark license compliance for headless SVG export
description:
## What / impact
The production SVG exporter embeds bpmn-js 17.11.1 in a headless page and returns `viewer.saveSVG()` output after sanitization. The dependency license has an additional requirement: source responsible for displaying the bpmn.io watermark must not be removed or changed, and the watermark must remain fully visible in an application. The returned SVG contains neither `bpmn.io` nor a watermark. Whether headless export falls within the requirement needs an explicit release decision; shipping without one creates avoidable license/compliance risk.

## Evidence
A real renderer export was 5,030 bytes and contained neither `bpmn.io` nor watermark text. `node_modules/bpmn-js/LICENSE` contains the mandatory watermark clause. Renderer code returns only the saved SVG root and allowlists a limited tag set.

## Where
- package.json/package-lock.json bpmn-js 17.11.1
- src/core/BpmnSvgRenderer.ts:11-13 and 85-195
- tests/integration/svg-export.test.ts
- packaged notices/license documentation

## Implementation direction
Have maintainers/legal choose and document one path: preserve a fully visible bpmn.io watermark in exported SVG and test it; obtain/record a license permitting watermark-free output; or replace bpmn-js rendering with a compatible alternative. If preserving it, update SVG sanitization deliberately without weakening external-resource/XSS controls and include all required notices in the package.

## Verification
Render a real diagram from the packed artifact and assert the chosen compliance invariant (visible safe watermark/link, recorded licensed mode, or no bpmn-js dependency). Review installed license text and npm tarball notices in CI; retain existing SVG safety tests.
acceptance_criteria: A documented maintainer/legal decision confirms the selected renderer and distribution comply with bpmn-js 17.11.1 terms; if bpmn-js remains, required watermark source/visibility is preserved in the served output or a valid alternative license is recorded; an integration test and package audit prevent accidental removal; user docs disclose any attribution behavior.
close_reason: Duplicate of mcp-bpmn-33g.6 created by a review command-substitution failure; all evidence and acceptance criteria are consolidated in mcp-bpmn-33g.6.
