title: LayoutModel/adapter layer has no production consumer (getLayoutModel, applyLayoutModel, bpmnDocumentToLayoutModel, MermaidAstLayoutAdapter geometry)
description:
## Evidence
src/core/layout/LayoutModel.ts:267-306, :660-681 (getLayoutModel/applyLayoutModel, normalizeLayoutModel), src/core/layout/adapters/BpmnDocumentLayoutAdapter.ts:22-282 (bpmnDocumentToLayoutModel), src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2122-2139, and both barrels (src/core/layout/index.ts, adapters/index.ts) are imported only by tests. MermaidAstLayoutAdapter's geometry is always overwritten (src/converters/MermaidConverter.ts:150-169; autoLayout:false is not exposed by any tool). positionLabels places 2-point edge labels at the target dock, which is unobservable. Beyond tracked mcp-bpmn-iqa.4 (which names files already deleted).

## Fix
Either wire the typed layout IR into auto_layout (the stated purpose of mcp-bpmn-3g8.1) or delete the unused adapters, barrels and their tests.
close_reason: Deleted the genuinely unreachable parts: both layout barrels, bpmnDocumentToLayoutModel, processContextToLayoutModel and mermaidAstToLayoutModel. MermaidAstLayoutAdapter.toLayoutModel and validateLayoutModel turned out to be production-reachable through SimpleBpmnGenerator, so the issue's premise held only in part. BpmnDocumentLayoutAdapter still hangs off the caller-less getLayoutModel/applyLayoutModel pair; tracked separately rather than removed here.

title: A second concurrent export svg fails with 'SVG renderer concurrency limit reached' instead of queueing
description:
## Evidence
Two parallel `export {format:"svg"}` calls -> ['ok', 'Error: SVG renderer concurrency limit reached'] (src/server/handlers.ts:197-199, :240-249 treat export as a snapshot read outside the mutation queue; src/core/BpmnSvgRenderer.ts:76-91). Two parallel save_svg calls both succeed. Behaviour is pinned by tests/integration/svg-export.test.ts.

## Fix
Bounded promise semaphore in runRender, or exclude svg export from the snapshot batch so it serializes like other calls.
close_reason: runRender now takes a bounded FIFO semaphore slot instead of throwing: overlapping exports queue, and only a wait list longer than maxQueuedRenders (default 32) is rejected. close() rejects waiters. Pinned by tests/integration/svg-export.test.ts (queueing, queue-limit, close-while-queued).

title: save_png has no scale/DPI option, silently downscales large diagrams, and reports only byteLength
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnSvgRenderer.ts:314-333 uses scale = Math.min(1, …) and no deviceScaleFactor; diagrams wider than 4096px are downscaled without notice (the 35-node scenario is already 2483px). The result (src/server/handlers.ts:1287-1293, src/server/tools.ts:822-828) carries only byteLength.

## Fix
Add scale (1-4) -> deviceScaleFactor; return width/height/scale/downscaled in the result.
close_reason: save_png gained scale (1-4, config MAX_PNG_SCALE) mapped to Puppeteer deviceScaleFactor, and the result now reports width, height, scale and downscaled. Large diagrams still downscale but say so in the message. Pinned by svg-export.test.ts and artifact-persistence.test.ts.

title: auto_layout exposes no options: no direction, spacing, subset, or pinned nodes; Mermaid TD comes out left-to-right
description:
## Evidence
src/server/tools.ts:1559-1568 accepts only algorithm:'horizontal'; src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2088-2120 replaces all DI; bpmn-auto-layout's layoutProcess(xml) takes no options. The same Mermaid diagram with TD/LR/BT/RL yields byte-identical BPMNDiagram output; skills/bpmn-modeler/references/capabilities.md:63 lists all five directions as supported input.

## Impact
Agents cannot ask for a vertical process, keep manually placed nodes, or lay out only a subprocess; anything they positioned by hand is discarded.

## Fix
Add direction (via transposition + re-docking), scopeId (layout a subset), pinnedElementIds, and spacing; until direction exists, warn when Mermaid direction != LR and fix capabilities.md.
close_reason: auto_layout gained the direction option named as the primary fix: left-to-right (default) and top-to-bottom, implemented as the transposition + re-docking the issue specified (src/core/layout/LayoutOrientation.ts). Pools become vertical bands with isHorizontal false, containers reflect whole so contents stay inside, ordinary shapes keep their proportions, and boundary events are re-attached. MermaidConverter now lays TD/TB/BT out downward and warns that BT/RL read back to front; capabilities.md and README corrected. spacing, scopeId and pinnedElementIds are not feasible against bpmn-auto-layout's option-free API and are tracked in mcp-bpmn-9sv.16.

title: auto_layout does not left-align pools and honours tool-default pool/lane sizes as lower bounds (~60% whitespace)
description:
## Evidence
Pools end at x=80 vs x=216 (route-pool scenario) and 280 vs 80 (collab-lanes); the policy translates y only (src/core/layout/CollaborationLayoutPolicy.ts:65-92, :115-133). The default 600x250 from add_pool (src/server/handlers.ts:800, :847; src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:360) is honoured as "requested": a one-row pool stays 250 tall and lanes are 240px for 80px of content, visible in the rendered PNGs.

## Fix
Align pool x to the minimum and equalize widths; honour only explicitly requested sizes (track whether size came from the agent or a default).
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. The oracle now resolves container ancestry by walking parentId, so shapes and labels never collide with their own pool, lane or expanded subprocess; bpmn:DataObject is registered non-visual; collinear/parallel edge overlap is reported and a shared dock is only excused between connectors of the same type. The router excludes scope ancestors from obstacles (so flows inside a subprocess route), treats a foreign participant as a hard obstacle for sequence flows, and steers message flows onto top/bottom docks. Pools are aligned to one left edge and width, and a pool size the caller never requested is no longer treated as a layout floor (size provenance is tracked through createElement). 3g8.4: the DI shape/edge arrays are hoisted out of the message-flow routing loop. 3g8.5, 5e7.4 and 5e7.5 were already implemented at HEAD; coverage was extended and the collinear blind spot in EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING closed.

title: add_pool stacks every pool at (100,100) when position is omitted, so everything before auto_layout overlaps
description:
## Evidence
Two add_pool calls without position both get position {x:100,y:100} (src/server/handlers.ts:799-800). Before layout: analyze_geometry -> `SHAPE_OVERLAP Participant_2 overlaps EndEvent_1`; update_element_geometry dry-run on StartEvent_1 -> `SHAPE_OVERLAP Participant_2 overlaps StartEvent_1`. The description says only "Position of the pool (optional)" (src/server/tools.ts:1175-1188).

## Fix
Stack new pools below the last participant (y = maxBottom + 50); document that omitted positions are placeholders replaced by auto_layout.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 8u0.10: new build_process tool creates many elements and their flows in one transaction, addressed by caller-chosen refs; the engine gained a batch mode so nested mutations join one lock, one serialization and one write, and a failure anywhere leaves the diagram untouched. 8u0.11: every failed call returns {code, message, recovery, ...context}; the advertised output schemas accept that shape, without which MCP clients reject error responses with -32602 once they have listed tools (this also fixed the pre-existing conflict errors). 3g8.12: pools stack below existing participants instead of all defaulting to (100,100). 33g.12: fast-uri and qs overridden to patched versions, both lockfiles regenerated and identical, npm audit clean.

title: Mermaid: 'subgraph Title' and 'subgraph "Title"' (Mermaid's primary forms) are rejected with a cascade of two errors per subgraph
description:
## Evidence
Valid `graph LR\n subgraph A\n a1[Start] --> a2[Task A]\n end` -> `2:10 [MALFORMED_SUBGRAPH] Expected subgraph syntax: subgraph <id>[<title>]` plus a spurious `4:3 [UNEXPECTED_SUBGRAPH_END]` for each end (the open subgraph is not pushed on a malformed declaration; src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:60, :133-161). Identical input with `subgraph A[Alpha]` succeeds. Neither README.md:223 nor skills/bpmn-modeler/references/workflows.md:36 / capabilities.md:68-70 say a [Title] is mandatory, and the skill tells agents to use one subgraph per participant.

## Fix
Accept `subgraph id[Title]`, `subgraph "Title"`, `subgraph Title` (derive/uniquify id from title); push the OpenSubgraph even on a malformed declaration; document the constraint until then.
close_reason: subgraph now accepts id[Title], id["Title"], "Title" and bare Title, deriving a unique ID from a title that has none. A malformed declaration pushes a placeholder so its end is not reported again: one error per problem instead of a cascade.

title: Mermaid: a non-gateway node with multiple outgoing edges converts to an implicit parallel split with no warning
description:
## Evidence
`A[Check] -->|ok| B[Ship]; A -->|fail| C[Refund]` converts with no warning to Task_A with two outgoing sequence flows: in BPMN a parallel (AND) split, so both branches execute, while the author meant an exclusive choice. Gateways are inferred only from {} (src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:628-647, src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts:163-191), never from topology.

## Impact
Silent semantic inversion that validate will not flag (it is legal BPMN).

## Fix
Emit IMPLICIT_PARALLEL_SPLIT at the node location when a non-decision node has >=2 outgoing edges (especially labeled), suggesting X{…}; optionally offer an option to synthesize an exclusive gateway.
close_reason: A non-decision node with two or more outgoing sequence flows now raises IMPLICIT_PARALLEL_SPLIT at that node's own line and column. Cross-subgraph message flows are excluded and the conversion output is unchanged, so the warning informs without changing behaviour.

title: Mermaid: unsupported bracket shapes ([(…)], [/…\], [\…/]) are silently mapped to a Task with delimiter garbage in the name
description:
## Evidence
`B[(DB)]` -> Task "(DB)", no warning; `B[/Manual\]` -> Task "/Manual\"; `C[\Para/]` -> Task "\Para/". The generic `^\[([^\]]+)\]` at src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:365-383 swallows any bracket shape. (Rounded, stadium and asymmetric shapes correctly error.)

## Fix
Match Mermaid's specific shape grammars before the generic rectangle; either map with a SHAPE_APPROXIMATED warning or reject with UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE naming the shape and the supported set.
close_reason: The shape table matches the longest delimiter first and rejects nine valid-but-unsupported Mermaid shapes plus the Mermaid 11 @{...} form with a new UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE error naming the supported replacement, instead of silently approximating them as a Task with delimiter garbage in the name.

title: Mermaid: common edge syntaxes (---, ==>, -- text -->, -. text .->, A --> B & C) fail with misleading 'malformed' errors
description:
## Evidence
`A --- B`, `A ==> B`, `A -- yes --> B` (Mermaid's primary labeled form), `B-. retry .->A`, `A --> B & C` all fail (src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:424-447, :322-329, :668-670). `B{{Prep}}` fails with misleading `2:24 Unexpected content after the target node` ({Prep matched decision, } left over). `B(Do work)` fails as `Malformed shape` though well-formed. Gaps are partly documented (capabilities.md:67) but the messages describe valid Mermaid as malformed.

## Fix
Extend parseConnector for -{2,}>, ={2,}>, `-- text -->`, `-. text .->`, `---` (warn) and & lists (cartesian product); for anything still unsupported use UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE/UNSUPPORTED_CONNECTOR with a "valid Mermaid, not in subset; use …" message.
close_reason: parseConnector now accepts -->, --->, ---, ==>, ===, -.-> and -.- with labels written inline or between pipes, expands & endpoint lists as a cartesian product, converts arrowless and thick links as directed sequence flows with a dropped-styling warning, and rejects ~~~, <-->, <==>, --o and --x with UNSUPPORTED_CONNECTOR.

title: Return structured error codes and recovery hints for all tool errors, not only revision conflicts
description:
## Evidence
src/server/handlers.ts:251-360 executeRequest attaches structuredContent (code, recovery) only for the five conflict/routing error classes; every other failure (No current diagram, Element X not found, Missing BPMN process owner, Invalid arguments…, Geometry collision rejected…, Unsafe geometry…) is a bare `Error: <message>` text with isError:true and no code.

## Impact
Agents must regex free text to branch on failures; hosts that surface structuredContent get nothing; the same condition is worded differently across tools.

## Fix
Define an error taxonomy (NO_CURRENT_DIAGRAM, ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND, CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARGUMENTS, OWNER_REQUIRED, SCOPE_MISMATCH, GEOMETRY_REJECTED, RENDER_UNAVAILABLE, FILE_EXISTS, …) with {code, message, recovery, ...context} in structuredContent for every isError result; pin it in the e2e schema test.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 8u0.10: new build_process tool creates many elements and their flows in one transaction, addressed by caller-chosen refs; the engine gained a batch mode so nested mutations join one lock, one serialization and one write, and a failure anywhere leaves the diagram untouched. 8u0.11: every failed call returns {code, message, recovery, ...context}; the advertised output schemas accept that shape, without which MCP clients reject error responses with -32602 once they have listed tools (this also fixed the pre-existing conflict errors). 3g8.12: pools stack below existing participants instead of all defaulting to (100,100). 33g.12: fast-uri and qs overridden to patched versions, both lockfiles regenerated and identical, npm audit clean.

title: Mermaid: quoted labels keep their surrounding quotes and a ']' inside quotes breaks parsing
description:
## Evidence
`B["Review (draft)"]` -> `<bpmn:task name=""Review (draft)"">`; same for markdown strings and `subgraph cust ["Customer Side"]` -> participant named `"Customer Side"` with literal quotes. `B["Check [urgent]"]` (valid Mermaid) -> `2:33 [MALFORMED_EDGE]`. src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:365-371, :60. README.md:230-231 claims labels round-trip unchanged.

## Fix
Try a quoted-string alternative first inside each shape delimiter (allowing ]/)/} inside) and use the unquoted content; optionally decode #quot;-style entity codes.
close_reason: Every Mermaid shape now tries a quoted body first, so quotes are delimiters and ], |, &, --> and markdown backticks inside them are kept as the label. Quoted labels decode #quot;/#35; entity codes; unquoted text stays verbatim. Subgraph titles use the same decoder. The assertion that expected the quotes to survive was updated deliberately.

title: Add a bulk build tool so a process with N nodes and M flows does not cost N+M round trips
description:
## Evidence
Every node and flow is a separate call (src/server/tools.ts add_event/add_activity/add_gateway/connect); a 12-step approval process with two gateways is ~30 sequential tool calls, each echoing the 95-char filename and revisions. Mermaid bootstrap (new_from_mermaid) is the only batch path but maps everything to plain bpmn:Task and cannot express user/service tasks, event definitions, conditions, or lanes, so agents still follow up with per-element update_element calls.

## Impact
Token cost and latency scale linearly with diagram size; agents using the server for anything beyond toy diagrams spend most of their budget on boilerplate.

## Fix
Add `build_process` / `apply_model_patch`: one call accepting {nodes:[{ref, kind, type, name, ownerId?, scopeId?, properties?, eventDefinition?}], flows:[{sourceRef, targetRef, label?, condition?, isDefault?}], lanes?:[…]} using client-side refs resolved to server IDs in the result, validated and applied atomically with the same rules as the single-element tools, followed by optional auto_layout.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 8u0.10: new build_process tool creates many elements and their flows in one transaction, addressed by caller-chosen refs; the engine gained a batch mode so nested mutations join one lock, one serialization and one write, and a failure anywhere leaves the diagram untouched. 8u0.11: every failed call returns {code, message, recovery, ...context}; the advertised output schemas accept that shape, without which MCP clients reject error responses with -32602 once they have listed tools (this also fixed the pre-existing conflict errors). 3g8.12: pools stack below existing participants instead of all defaulting to (100,100). 33g.12: fast-uri and qs overridden to patched versions, both lockfiles regenerated and identical, npm audit clean.

title: No tool can set bpmn:documentation on any element
description:
## Evidence
`grep -i documentation src/server/tools.ts src/server/handlers.ts src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts src/core/BpmnDocument.ts` -> no matches in the tool surface or engine mutations. Import preserves existing <bpmn:documentation> (verified), but add_*/update_element cannot create or edit it.

## Impact
bpmn:documentation is the standard place for step descriptions, acceptance criteria and rationale; agents modelling a process from a spec have nowhere to put the text except annotations, which clutter the diagram.

## Fix
Add optional `documentation` (string, bounded) to add_event/add_activity/add_gateway/add_pool/add_lane/connect/update_element/update_connection; return it from get_element/get_connection; serialize as <bpmn:documentation> (textFormat text/plain).
close_reason: documentation is now a first-class field on add_event, add_activity, add_gateway, connect and update_element; BpmnDocument.applyDocumentation writes bpmn:Documentation and import reads it back, and assertElementProperties accepts it as a supported property.

title: README examples hard-code element IDs the server never generates (Example 2 fails on a fresh server)
description:
## Evidence
README.md:869-898 Example 2 does new_from_mermaid then `update_element {elementId:"UserTask_1", properties:{assignee:"reviewer"}}`; the Mermaid import actually creates StartEvent_A, Task_B, Gateway_C, Task_D, Task_E, EndEvent_F (all bpmn:Task) and the call returns `Element UserTask_1 not found`; even with the right ID, assignee is rejected on bpmn:Task. Example 1 (README.md:854-863) hard-codes StartEvent_1, UserTask_1… which hold only on a fresh server; failed attempts consume counters (src/utils/IdGenerator.ts:9-13).

## Fix
Capture and reuse returned elementIds in the examples; note that Mermaid nodes become plain bpmn:Task with <Type>_<mermaidId> IDs.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 33g.10: the README heading, the packed tool list and the pinned fingerprints all derive from a generated scripts/tool-contract.json refreshed by 'npm run contract:update'; an in-process test catches drift without a pack cycle; two stale geometry baselines were re-pinned to the diagnostics the imperfect fixture genuinely produces, and the corrected-collaboration baseline is now empty because the workflow's own repair resolves the semantic error. npm run test:package passes end to end. 33g.13: version set to 0.3.0 across package.json and both plugin manifests, with a dated CHANGELOG section covering the five undocumented commits and all 12 previously unmentioned tools; nothing was tagged. 33g.14: README examples capture and reuse returned element IDs and state the real Mermaid-derived IDs; both were replayed against a live server.

title: connect's description and README deny the message-flow inference that actually happens
description:
## Evidence
connect across pools -> connectionType "bpmn:MessageFlow"; to a black-box participant -> MessageFlow_3 (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:676-688). Tool description (src/server/tools.ts:1141): "Connect two elements in the current diagram"; README.md:426: "Connect two elements with a sequence flow"; README.md:186: "Direct connect authors sequence flows; Mermaid subgraphs can also produce message flows". SKILL.md:26 says the opposite.

## Fix
Description: "SequenceFlow between flow nodes in the same process/scope, or MessageFlow when endpoints are in different participants (collaboration only); label = flow name; condition/isDefault apply to SequenceFlow only." Fix README 186/426; optionally add an explicit connectionType parameter.
close_reason: connect's tool description now states that endpoints in one process get a SequenceFlow and endpoints in different participants of a collaboration get a MessageFlow, and that condition/isDefault are sequence-flow only. README's connect section, the tool-area table, and the Known Limitations entry were corrected to match; the limitation is now the real one, that the type is inferred and cannot be requested.

title: connect's 'Source or target element not found' does not say which endpoint is missing
description:
## Evidence
`connect {sourceId:"Nope_1",…}` and `connect {…, targetId:"Nope_1"}` both return the identical `Error: Source or target element not found` (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:672; reused by update_connection at :1178).

## Impact
The most common agent mistake (stale or mistyped ID) costs an extra round trip to locate.

## Fix
`Source element "Nope_1" not found` / `Target element "Nope_1" not found`; if the ID is a connection, say so.
close_reason: connect now raises missingEndpointError(context, side, elementId), which names whether the source or the target is missing, gives the id, and says when the id exists but is not a flow node. Pinned in tests/integration/handlers.test.ts.

title: update_connection is the only mutation that requires a revision, forcing a get_connection round trip for a label change
description:
## Evidence
`update_connection {connectionId:"Flow_3", label:"Approved"}` -> `expectedRevision or expectedSemanticRevision is required` (src/server/tools.ts:1314-1316; src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:1157). No other mutation requires a revision; all return afterRevision, and update_connection accepts expectedRevision from any prior result. The skill codifies the two-step (skills/bpmn-modeler/SKILL.md:28).

## Fix
Make both guards optional like every other tool (keep compare-and-set when supplied); at minimum state in the description that afterRevision from the previous mutation suffices.
close_reason: The mandatory-revision superRefine on update_connection was removed from tools.ts and the matching guard from SimpleBpmnEngine.updateConnection. A label change is now a single call; expectedRevision and expectedSemanticRevision remain available for callers that want the optimistic guard.

title: save_as error tells the agent to 'use overwrite option' but save_as has no overwrite parameter
description:
## Evidence
`save_as {filename:"approval.bpmn"}` (existing) -> `Error: File already exists: approval.bpmn. Use overwrite option to replace.` (src/utils/FileManager.ts:220). The save_as schema (src/server/tools.ts:953-961) has only filename/expectedRevision and is strict, so overwrite:true is rejected.

## Fix
Add overwrite:boolean (default false) to save_as like save_svg/save_png, or reword to "choose another filename or delete_diagram_file first".
close_reason: save_as gained the overwrite parameter its error message already advertised. The handler threads it through commitMutation's replaceTarget, reports previousFilename and removedPreviousFile, and a generated placeholder filename is replaced rather than left orphaned.

title: list_elements.elementType is free text, so 'userTask' silently returns zero results
description:
## Evidence
`list_elements {elementType:"userTask"}` -> count 0, no error; `{elementType:"bpmn:UserTask"}` -> 2 results. Schema is a free-form identifier() described only as "Filter by element type (optional)" (src/server/tools.ts:1220); handler does exact match on e.type (src/server/handlers.ts:870-875); README.md:485.

## Impact
Agents reuse the activityType/gatewayType vocabulary they just used and silently get an empty list.

## Fix
z.enum of flow-node ∪ artifact ∪ bpmn:Participant|bpmn:Lane|bpmn:Association types (self-documenting in tools/list), or accept the short aliases via TypeMappings and error on unknown values.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 8u0.1: the expanded XML NCName character class is validated by a refinement instead of an advertised pattern, taking tools/list from 168 KB to 129 KB; a contract test bounds the size and proves NCName is still enforced. 8u0.2: new_bpmn/new_from_mermaid/open_mermaid_file accept a filename, and save_as removes a server-generated placeholder while never removing a caller-chosen name. 8u0.3: delete_element reports removedElementIds/removedElementCount and the description states container cascade. 8u0.4: elementType is an enum of every listable BPMN type. 8u0.5: get_element points at get_connection for connection ids and names the rendered reference for a backing DataObject.

title: get_element says 'not found' for connection IDs and the backing DataObject ID that other tools return
description:
## Evidence
`get_element {elementId:"Flow_3"}` -> `Error: Element Flow_3 not found` although delete_element accepts that ID and get_element already answers for Associations (src/server/handlers.ts:909-924). `get_element {elementId:"DataObject_1"}` -> not found although add_data_object returned that ID.

## Fix
Serve connections from get_element (as with associations) or answer `Flow_3 is a bpmn:SequenceFlow; use get_connection`; for DataObject_*: `non-rendered backing object of DataObjectReference_1`.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 8u0.1: the expanded XML NCName character class is validated by a refinement instead of an advertised pattern, taking tools/list from 168 KB to 129 KB; a contract test bounds the size and proves NCName is still enforced. 8u0.2: new_bpmn/new_from_mermaid/open_mermaid_file accept a filename, and save_as removes a server-generated placeholder while never removing a caller-chosen name. 8u0.3: delete_element reports removedElementIds/removedElementCount and the description states container cascade. 8u0.4: elementType is an enum of every listable BPMN type. 8u0.5: get_element points at get_connection for connection ids and names the rendered reference for a backing DataObject.

title: delete_element silently removes contained nodes when deleting a pool/subprocess and only reports connection counts
description:
## Evidence
`delete_element {elementId:"Participant_1"}` -> `Deleted element Participant_1 and 6 associated connections`, removedConnectionCount 6; element count dropped 13->9: four flow nodes of the owned process vanished unmentioned. `delete_element SubProcess_1` -> "and 2 associated connections" while nested Task_3 also vanished. Description (src/server/tools.ts:1484-1492) says only "cascading incident connections"; README.md:665 likewise. Engine: src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:1732-1770.

## Impact
Agents under-report destruction; the skill's "tell the user when deleting will cascade" rule cannot be honoured.

## Fix
Add removedElementIds/removedElementCount to output and text; state in the description that deleting a participant/subprocess/transaction/lane removes contained elements.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. 8u0.1: the expanded XML NCName character class is validated by a refinement instead of an advertised pattern, taking tools/list from 168 KB to 129 KB; a contract test bounds the size and proves NCName is still enforced. 8u0.2: new_bpmn/new_from_mermaid/open_mermaid_file accept a filename, and save_as removes a server-generated placeholder while never removing a caller-chosen name. 8u0.3: delete_element reports removedElementIds/removedElementCount and the description states container cascade. 8u0.4: elementType is an enum of every listable BPMN type. 8u0.5: get_element points at get_connection for connection ids and names the rendered reference for a backing DataObject.

title: .mcp-bpmn.json is not a containment boundary and select_workspace silently creates directory trees
description:
## Evidence
src/config/WorkspaceSession.ts:73-82 sets startupBoundary = launchCwd even with repository config; activateSelection (:113-129) only checks that boundary; canonicalDescendant (:202-227) mkdirSync's every missing segment. Probe with `{"path":"wiki/assets"}`: `select_workspace {path:"src"}` succeeded; `select_workspace {path:"brand/new/dirs"}` created three directories and new_bpmn wrote there. The tool description (src/server/tools.ts:1596-1603) says nothing about creating directories; README.md:836-846 says the config "narrows storage".

## Impact
Repo-pinned storage is unenforced; hallucinated paths litter the repo with empty directories, undisclosed to the model.

## Fix
Use the configured workspace as the boundary when source === 'repository_config'; fail on non-existent paths (or require explicit create:true) and say so in the description; document in README.
close_reason: The configured workspace, not the launch cwd, is now the startup boundary for both repository_config and environment sources, and resolveSelection no longer creates directories unless the caller passes create:true. select_workspace's description and schema now say the directory must already exist, and the boundary error is classified as file_not_found with a recovery hint. New tests/security/workspace-containment.test.ts pins both halves; three assertions that encoded the old behaviour were updated deliberately.

title: Validator does not enforce condition/default-flow rules that the engine enforces on its own mutations
description:
## Evidence
validateSequenceFlows (src/core/BpmnValidator.ts:324-361) checks only endpoints/scope. Conditional flow out of a parallel gateway -> passed; `<bpmn:exclusiveGateway default="f1">` where f1 is s->g (another node's flow) -> passed; default flow that also has a condition -> passed. The engine enforces all three for its own mutations (supportsConditionalOutgoingFlow, reconcileConditionalAndDefaultFlows), so violating imports validate clean but later connect/update_connection fail with serializer errors the agent cannot explain.

## Fix
Add rules: conditionExpression only from Activity / Exclusive|Inclusive|Complex gateway; default must be an outgoing flow of the same node; default flow has no condition; Parallel/EventBased gateways have no default.
close_reason: The validator gained validateFlowCondition and validateDefaultFlows, matching the rules the engine already enforced on its own mutations. validateDefaultFlows also inspects node.$attrs.default, which is where moddle puts the attribute on imported documents.

title: A stale compare-and-write lock directory permanently blocks autosave for that file (5 s stall then failure, across restarts)
description:
## Evidence
src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts:117-129, :197-229 acquireLock() = mkdir('.mcp-bpmn-lock-<sha256>'), retried 500x10 ms then `busy`; no pid/mtime/staleness reclaim. The lock is held across read+rename and the worker can be killed there (child.kill() at :499, forced process.exit(1) at the shutdown deadline in src/server/index.ts:112-118, OOM). Reproduced: `compareAndWrite failed after 5177 ms: busy Diagram file is busy`; the lock dir remains.

## Impact
After one crash, every mutation on that diagram stalls 5 s and fails forever, across restarts, until the user deletes a hidden directory no doc mentions.

## Fix
Put pid+timestamp in the lock with stale reclaim, or drop the lock and verify after rename; document the lock dir; name the lock path in the busy error.
close_reason: SafeFilePath's compare-and-write lock now carries an owner record (uuid, pid, host, time). A lock whose pid is dead on this host, or older than 30s, is reclaimed through an O_EXCL claim keyed to the exact holder record, and assertLockHeld runs immediately before the destructive rename so a writer that lost its lock can never publish. The busy error names the lock directory. Pinned by five cases in tests/unit/utils/SafeFilePath.test.ts.

title: Persistence failures surface as an opaque 'Unable to save BPMN file' with no path or cause; root is cached forever
description:
## Evidence
The worker collapses EACCES/EROFS/EPERM (e.g. fs.link on no-hardlink filesystems) and root-identity `changed` into `access` (src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts:240-245, :397-407); FileManager (src/utils/FileManager.ts:207-225) maps that to the literal string. resolveRoot() caches forever except not_found. Reproduced: after rm -rf + recreate of the workspace, every save returns `Unable to save BPMN file` until restart. new_bpmn autosaves immediately (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2058-2068), so an unwritable launch cwd (clients that spawn with cwd `/`) makes the server unusable; README.md:66-79 does not warn. deleteDiagram() likewise hides not_found.

## Fix
Include the workspace path and a coarse cause in errors; re-resolve the root when the pinned one disappears; README note for cwd-inheriting clients.
close_reason: Persistence failures now name the file, the workspace and the cause (FileManager.describeStorageFailure), built from errno symbols only so no path or content leaks through Node's message. The pinned root is revalidated before every operation and re-pinned only when the configured path is not a symlink, so a recreated workspace no longer needs a restart. Read errors deliberately stay path-free.

title: bpmn:incoming/bpmn:outgoing lists are not maintained for flows added to imported documents
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnDocument.ts reconcileConnectionReferences (:1009-1021) only moves existing incoming/outgoing entries on rewire; attachConnection (:1238-1251, :1185-1206) never adds them for new flows. After connect(c, e) on an imported file: task c has `<bpmn:incoming>f2</bpmn:incoming>` but no outgoing; endEvent e lacks the new Flow_1. Imported Gateway_1 lists Flow_yes, Flow_no but not new Flow_5.

## Impact
Partially populated derived lists contradict sourceRef/targetRef. bpmn-js and Camunda 7 recompute, but linters/importers that trust these lists see an inconsistent model; diffs are noisy.

## Fix
When attaching a new sequence flow in the retained path, push into outgoing/incoming if the endpoint already uses those arrays; or strip all incoming/outgoing on import for consistency.
close_reason: registerConnectionOnEndpoints maintains bpmn:incoming and bpmn:outgoing for flows added to imported documents whenever either endpoint already uses that convention.

title: Validator and connect accept illegal event-based gateway targets
description:
## Evidence
No rule in src/core/BpmnValidator.ts (:324-361, :448-549) inspects bpmn:EventBasedGateway; "event-based gateway targeting a user task" -> Validation passed: 0 errors. SimpleBpmnEngine.connect also allows it.

## Impact
Invalid model (targets must be intermediate catch events with message/timer/signal/conditional definitions, or receive tasks) reported valid; Camunda deployment fails later.

## Fix
Add a rule requiring targets of event-based gateway outgoing flows to be bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent (allowed definitions) or bpmn:ReceiveTask; enforce in connect too.
close_reason: Added EVENT_BASED_GATEWAY_TARGET_DEFINITIONS with isEventBasedGatewayTarget in the engine and validateEventBasedGatewayTarget in the validator, so an illegal target is rejected by connect and reported by validate.

title: Imported compensation boundary events cannot be updated: moddle defaults captured as authored payload
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:2187-2192, :2210-2212 readFlowNode copies definition.waitForCompletion and item.cancelActivity whenever typeof boolean; moddle returns descriptor defaults (true) for absent attributes. A bpmn-js-style `<bpmn:boundaryEvent attachedToRef="t"><bpmn:compensateEventDefinition/></bpmn:boundaryEvent>` imports as {"eventDefinitionPayload":{"waitForCompletion":true},"cancelActivity":true}; `rename comp boundary FAILED: Compensation activityRef/waitForCompletion is only valid on throwing events` (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:3390-3394, :3191-3193).

## Fix
Copy waitForCompletion/cancelActivity only when explicitly present in the source; never capture waitForCompletion for boundary events.
close_reason: Moddle's materialized schema defaults (waitForCompletion, cancelActivity, textFormat, calledElementBinding) are no longer captured as authored payload, and waitForCompletion is deleted rather than assigned undefined so the serializer cannot emit the literal string 'undefined'.

title: Validator flags every mainstream-tool compensation boundary event that omits cancelActivity
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnValidator.ts:520-528: `definitionType === 'bpmn:CompensateEventDefinition' && event.cancelActivity !== false` -> error. bpmn-js and Camunda Modeler never write cancelActivity="false" for compensation boundary events, so the moddle default true triggers BPMN_INVALID_BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTION on a minimal bpmn-js-style file.

## Fix
Raise only when the attribute is explicitly present and true; relax the engine-side cancelActivity !== false rule likewise.
close_reason: The compensation-boundary rule now fires only when cancelActivity is explicitly written in the source XML, detected by elementIdsDeclaringAttribute. The pinned false positive on the Camunda C7 fixture was removed.

title: Text annotation text cannot be edited; update_element name on a TextAnnotation succeeds but changes nothing visible
description:
## Evidence
`update_element {elementId:"TextAnnotation_1", properties:{text:"New text"}}` -> `Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'text'` (elementUpdateProperties, src/server/tools.ts:383-392). `update_element {…, name:"New text"}` -> success, but get_element shows name "New text" alongside properties {"text":"Note",…}. The engine already supports text/textFormat properties (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:3078-3090); only the zod schema blocks them.

## Impact
Fixing an annotation typo means delete + recreate (+ its association); `name` misleads agents into thinking they edited it.

## Fix
Add text/textFormat to elementUpdateProperties; reject name for bpmn:TextAnnotation or map it to text.
close_reason: update_element accepts text and textFormat in properties; BpmnDocument writes bpmn:TextAnnotation/text and defaults textFormat to text/plain on both sides of the comparison so a round trip no longer reports a spurious semantic difference.

title: Actionable import errors are collapsed into 'Failed to parse BPMN XML: malformed or invalid input'
description:
## Evidence
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2994-3020 safeImportError forwards only regex-matched messages; everything else becomes the generic text. Observed for the calledElement QName error, `Data object reference dor crosses data object scope`, and `… has an invalid dataObjectRef`. These messages are generated by this code base and contain no file content.

## Impact
Agents cannot tell the user what to change in a well-formed file.

## Fix
Pass through engine-generated structural messages (allowlist by error class rather than regex); reserve the generic text for genuine XML parser exceptions.
close_reason: safeImportError was inverted: structural messages are forwarded verbatim and the generic 'malformed or invalid input' text is used only for a genuine BpmnXmlParseError, which BpmnDocument now throws from the XML-parse boundary.

title: update_element on a start event inside an imported event subprocess fails even for a rename
description:
## Evidence
src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:3179-3181 assertElementProperties runs on every updateElement with the merged existing properties and rejects eventDefinition on any start event whose scopeId !== ownerId; the typed model never records triggeredByEvent (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:2145-2247). `rename EventSub_Start FAILED: Start events in regular subprocesses cannot have an event definition` when only name was changed.

## Fix
Read triggeredByEvent into subprocess properties on import; exempt start events whose scope is an event subprocess; only enforce the rule when the update actually sets eventDefinition.
close_reason: assertElementProperties exempts start events whose containing scope has triggeredByEvent true, so a rename inside an imported event subprocess succeeds. triggeredByEvent is captured on import, written back on serialize, and listed as a supported property.

title: update_connection accepts a label on Associations, reports success, then silently drops it on save
description:
## Evidence
`update_connection {connectionId:"Association_1", label:"LOSTLABEL", expectedRevision:…}` -> success with after.label "LOSTLABEL"; get_connection shows the label; but the export XML lacks it and after close + open_bpmn get_connection returns label undefined. bpmn:Association has no name attribute, so `semantic.name = connection.label` (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:1006, via src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:1279) is discarded by moddle. Schema at src/server/tools.ts:1281-1283 allows it.

## Impact
Silent data loss with a success response; memory and file disagree until the next open.

## Fix
Throw `Labels are only valid on SequenceFlow and MessageFlow` for associations in updateConnection and say so in the schema description.
close_reason: updateConnection now rejects a label on a bpmn:Association instead of reporting success and dropping it on save. The assertion that encoded the old behaviour was updated deliberately.

title: Mermaid Conversion Fidelity — parse what agents actually write
description:
## Scope
new_from_mermaid / open_mermaid_file reject or silently mangle common, valid Mermaid flowchart syntax that LLMs emit (semicolons, quoted labels, `subgraph Title`, `-- text -->`, `&` fan-out) and make semantically wrong mapping choices (implicit parallel splits, name loss on start/end substrings). Findings verified with a 50-snippet harness against dist/.

## Success Criteria
- Canonical Mermaid docs examples parse or fail with an error that says "valid Mermaid, unsupported subset: use X".
- No silent name loss or silent shape mis-typing.
- Diagnostics carry correct line/column and reference Mermaid node IDs, not generated BPMN IDs.

title: placeMessageLabel does not treat peer message-flow labels as obstacles — labels can overlap each other
description: routeCollaborationConnections() in src/core/layout/CollaborationLayoutPolicy.ts builds labelObstacles from element and lane bounds (lines 303-307) but does not include the label bounds of already-routed message flows. When multiple message flows exist between the same pair of participants, their labels are placed independently using the same candidate set (midpoints along the same horizontal/vertical segments), so they will often land on identical or near-identical positions. The placeMessageLabel fallback (line 384-391) places the label at outer.right + gap, which means all fallback labels also stack at the same coordinate. Fix: accumulate placed label bounds into labelObstacles before each subsequent call.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. The oracle now resolves container ancestry by walking parentId, so shapes and labels never collide with their own pool, lane or expanded subprocess; bpmn:DataObject is registered non-visual; collinear/parallel edge overlap is reported and a shared dock is only excused between connectors of the same type. The router excludes scope ancestors from obstacles (so flows inside a subprocess route), treats a foreign participant as a hard obstacle for sequence flows, and steers message flows onto top/bottom docks. Pools are aligned to one left edge and width, and a pool size the caller never requested is no longer treated as a layout floor (size provenance is tracked through createElement). 3g8.4: the DI shape/edge arrays are hoisted out of the message-flow routing loop. 3g8.5, 5e7.4 and 5e7.5 were already implemented at HEAD; coverage was extended and the collinear blind spot in EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING closed.

title: AnchoredFileWorker: 100ms idle timeout causes constant subprocess churn under normal load
description: The ANCHORED_FILE_WORKER inline script in src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts arms a 100ms idle exit timer after each operation and on startup. At any inter-request gap longer than 100ms the worker process exits, and the next file operation (read, write, delete) must restart it and wait for the ready handshake before proceeding. Under normal MCP usage where diagram operations arrive more than 100ms apart, every file operation effectively cold-starts the worker. The SafeFileStore.workerFor() and runWithRetry() mechanics hide the restart, but the latency penalty and process churn are real. Increasing the idle timeout to ~5 s (or making it configurable via the ResourceLimits struct) would eliminate most restarts without holding resources open for long.
close_reason: Already fixed earlier in this release cycle: ANCHORED_FILE_WORKER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS is 5s (src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts:54), not 100ms, so a worker survives ordinary inter-request gaps. Pinned by tests/unit/utils/SafeFilePath.test.ts 'reuses its anchored worker across ordinary request gaps', which asserts the child pid is unchanged across a 250ms gap. Left the timeout a constant rather than a ResourceLimits field: no caller has a reason to tune it and the issue offered that as an alternative, not a requirement.

title: BpmnSvgRenderer: new browser process per render call — no reuse across exports
description: BpmnSvgRenderer.render() calls this.launchBrowser() every invocation (src/core/BpmnSvgRenderer.ts:65) and closes the browser in the finally block of renderWithBrowser() (line 98). Each Puppeteer browser launch takes 1–3 seconds. For an AI agent workflow that exports SVG repeatedly (e.g. after each diagram edit), every export pays full browser-start overhead. The maxConcurrentRenders=1 default serialises renders, so the overhead compounds. Keeping a long-lived browser page alive between renders (launching lazily on first call, reusing the existing browser until close() is called) would reduce per-export latency by roughly 90% for warm calls.
close_reason: Already fixed earlier in this release cycle: BpmnSvgRenderer caches this.browser and getBrowser() reuses it across renders, relaunching only after a disconnect. Pinned by svg-export.test.ts 'reuses one browser without leaking render pages until shutdown', which asserts launchBrowser is called once for two exports.

title: Dead code: LayoutEngine.ts and AutoLayout.ts are never imported in production
description: src/core/LayoutEngine.ts defines a LayoutEngine class and imports MermaidAstLayoutAdapter; it is only referenced in tests/unit/core/LayoutModel.test.ts and is never used from any production source file. src/utils/AutoLayout.ts defines an AutoLayout class that is also never imported anywhere — neither in production nor tests. Both files survive from earlier prototyping and now misrepresent the actual layout architecture (production delegates all layout to bpmn-auto-layout via BpmnAutoLayoutV2Adapter). They should be deleted to avoid developer confusion and to keep dead-code scanners clean.
close_reason: LayoutEngine.ts and AutoLayout.ts were already deleted; what remained was the leftover jest.config.js coverage ignore for a file that no longer exists and two docs claiming a second layout path. Both removed, and IMPLEMENTATION.md and engine-contract.md now record that there is one layout path.

title: CollaborationLayoutPolicy: shapeFor/edgeFor do O(n) linear scan inside message-flow routing loop
description: routeCollaborationConnections() in src/core/layout/CollaborationLayoutPolicy.ts calls shapeFor() and edgeFor() for every connection it routes (lines 347, 350). Each helper does Array.from(document.diagram.shapes.values()).find(...), an O(M) scan over all DI shapes. For a collaboration with N message flows and M total shapes, routing is O(N×M). For a diagram near the configured limits (2000 elements, many message flows), this can become slow. Build a Map<elementId, shape> and Map<connectionId, edge> once before the loop and replace .find() calls with O(1) Map lookups.
close_reason: Fixed in 09e25f8. The oracle now resolves container ancestry by walking parentId, so shapes and labels never collide with their own pool, lane or expanded subprocess; bpmn:DataObject is registered non-visual; collinear/parallel edge overlap is reported and a shared dock is only excused between connectors of the same type. The router excludes scope ancestors from obstacles (so flows inside a subprocess route), treats a foreign participant as a hard obstacle for sequence flows, and steers message flows onto top/bottom docks. Pools are aligned to one left edge and width, and a pool size the caller never requested is no longer treated as a layout floor (size provenance is tracked through createElement). 3g8.4: the DI shape/edge arrays are hoisted out of the message-flow routing loop. 3g8.5, 5e7.4 and 5e7.5 were already implemented at HEAD; coverage was extended and the collinear blind spot in EDGE_EDGE_CROSSING closed.

title: Correct README installation, capability, dependency, and performance claims
description:
## What / impact
README.md contains multiple materially false release-facing claims. Users following it can clone placeholder URLs, configure a bundle not produced by the default build, expect a browser-free/lightweight server despite production Puppeteer, and rely on “Complete BPMN 2.0”/“Enterprise-Ready” language that exceeds the implemented subset.

## Evidence
- Lines 25 and 743-744 use `github.com/your-org/...` instead of the actual repository.
- Client examples use `dist/server/bundle.cjs`, but `npm run build` only runs tsc; the bundle requires a separate script.
- Lines 631/697 claim no browser/heavy dependency, while Puppeteer is production runtime for SVG.
- Line 698 claims ~48KB CommonJS without a reproducible metric; the current artifact/dependency footprint is materially larger.
- Lines 11/16 claim complete BPMN 2.0 and enterprise readiness despite known unsupported/gapped contracts.

## Where
README.md throughout, especially lines 11-25, 50-70, 620-705, 743-744; package.json scripts/dependencies; public tool schema and engine contract.

## Implementation direction
Rewrite from verified behavior and commands. Separate source-clone versus npm-package setup, ESM bin versus optional CJS bundle, portable versus Camunda profile, and authoring subset versus full BPMN. Document Puppeteer/browser installation and SVG limitations. Generate or test commands/links and record measured artifact sizes with the exact command/date rather than permanent marketing numbers.

## Verification
Run every documented command in clean source and temp packed-package environments; link-check repository URLs; compare capability tables against tools/list and contract tests; verify browser/no-browser paths and recompute any published size metric.
acceptance_criteria: Every install/build/client command works from a clean clone and packed artifact; repository links target oisee/mcp-bpmn; capability statements match the advertised/tested tool matrix; dependency and bundle-size claims are measured against the release artifact; unsupported/partial features and browser requirements are explicit.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: corrected README setup, capability, dependency, browser, link, and measured release-artifact claims with executable drift checks

title: Replace stale engine-contract TODOs with executable regression tests
description:
## What / impact
The canonical engine-contract suite still contains five `test.todo` placeholders. Four capabilities (lanes, SVG, extensionElements preservation, and validation/conditions) are implemented and covered elsewhere, so the supposed contract gate does not protect them. The fifth hides the real advertised-but-unsupported vertical layout bug. This leaves release confidence dependent on scattered tests rather than the declared interface matrix.

## Evidence
`tests/contracts/engine-contract.test.ts:439-443` reports G1-G5 as TODO. The full test run therefore passes with five unexecuted contract cases even though G4 is a known failure.

## Where
- tests/contracts/engine-contract.test.ts:1-443
- tests/fixtures/engine-contract
- renderer Jest project/config
- existing focused lane, SVG, import-roundtrip, and validation tests

## Implementation direction
Convert each TODO into a minimal production-path contract assertion. Reuse fixture/helpers rather than copying entire focused suites. Put browser-backed G2 in the renderer project if needed but keep one explicit contract command/gate. Make G4 depend on the vertical-layout contract decision, not an unconditional skip.

## Verification

title: Support deleting sequence and message flows without deleting endpoint nodes
description:
## What / impact
The server can create sequence and message flows but exposes no operation to remove one independently. `delete_element` only special-cases associations; for normal connections it falls through to engine element deletion and reports not found. Users must delete an endpoint node (and all incident connections) to correct a mistaken flow, making the authoring surface incomplete and destructive.

## Evidence
After creating StartEvent -> Task, `connect` returned `Flow_1`. Calling `delete_element({elementId:'Flow_1'})` returned `isError:true`, “Element Flow_1 not found.” There is no disconnect/delete-flow tool in the advertised inventory or engine API.

## Where
- src/server/tools.ts:599-605
- src/server/handlers.ts:721-739
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:660-766
- BpmnDocument connection/DI/default-flow handling
- engine contract and e2e authoring flows

## Implementation direction
Prefer extending `delete_element` to delete any BaseElement/connection ID consistently, or add one clearly named `delete_connection` tool if protocol compatibility requires it. In one transaction remove sequence/message flow semantics and BPMNEdge, clear source `defaultFlow` when applicable, preserve endpoints, serialize, validate, and autosave. Keep association behavior aligned.

## Verification
Table-test sequence, message, association, conditional, and default flows; delete each by ID and assert endpoints survive, incoming/outgoing counts and defaultFlow update, XML/DI omit the edge, persisted reopen matches, and injected write failure rolls back all state. Add strict MCP e2e coverage.
acceptance_criteria: A public tool can delete sequence flows and message flows by ID while preserving both endpoints; deletion removes semantic and DI edge state, clears any source defaultFlow reference, autosaves atomically, and round-trips; deleting an unknown or unsupported connection returns a stable error with no mutation.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: delete_element atomically removes sequence, message, association, conditional, and default flows while preserving endpoints, clearing defaults, removing semantic/DI state, autosaving, and rolling back on failure

title: Handle SIGTERM with bounded graceful shutdown and in-flight cleanup
description:
## What / impact
The executable handles SIGINT only. Containers, service managers, and `npm` commonly terminate with SIGTERM. Under SIGTERM Node exits by signal immediately, with no server/transport close, no bounded drain of active autosave operations, and no coordinated cleanup of Puppeteer/layout subprocesses. This risks partial user-visible operations and orphaned child processes.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Spawn the built stdio server and complete MCP initialize.
2. Send SIGTERM to the child process.
3. Observe exit by signal with no shared shutdown/drain path; repeat during a delayed child-backed operation.

## Evidence
After MCP initialize, sending SIGTERM to the server produced `{code:null, signal:'SIGTERM'}`. No shutdown hook ran; src/server/index.ts installs only `process.on('SIGINT')`.

## Where
- src/server/index.ts:41-65
- BpmnSvgRenderer browser lifecycle
- src/core/layout/BpmnLayoutAdapter.ts subprocess lifecycle
- tests/e2e server process harness

## Implementation direction
Implement one idempotent shutdown coordinator for SIGINT, SIGTERM, transport close/EOF, and fatal startup errors. Stop accepting calls, await tracked in-flight handlers and their persistence, close server/transport/renderers/layout children, then exit; enforce a documented hard timeout and meaningful nonzero exit on forced shutdown. Avoid calling process.exit before awaited cleanup settles.

## Verification
Spawn the real built server, begin delay-injected save/layout/render calls, send SIGTERM and SIGINT, and assert deterministic exit codes, committed-or-rolled-back files, closed pipes/browser/layout child PIDs, no open handles, and safe behavior on two rapid signals and startup failure.
acceptance_criteria: SIGINT, SIGTERM, transport EOF, and startup failure use one idempotent shutdown path; accepted in-flight mutations finish or roll back before exit within a documented timeout; renderer/layout child processes are closed; repeated signals cannot double-close; process-level tests assert clean exit and no orphan children.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: unified bounded shutdown drains accepted persistence, closes renderer/layout children, handles SIGINT/SIGTERM/EOF/startup failure idempotently, and has process-level coverage

title: Enforce XML NCName rules for every BPMN xsd:ID
description:
## What / impact
BPMN IDs are XML Schema `xsd:ID`, whose lexical space is NCName (no colon, valid start/continuation characters). The serializer, importer, engine element IDs, and validator currently enforce uniqueness/references but not NCName syntax. They can emit and bless XML that downstream BPMN tools reject or cannot reference reliably.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create/import a BPMN element whose ID is a:b.
2. Serialize and reopen the document.
3. Run syntax/semantic/full validation and observe no invalid-xsd-ID issue.

## Evidence
Creating an element with `id:'a:b'` succeeded; export contained the ID, bpmn-moddle parsed it, and all validator levels returned no issue (`serialized:true`, `syntaxValid:true`, `issues:[]`). The existing QName helper is only for callable references and intentionally allows one colon, so it cannot validate IDs.

## Where
- src/core/BpmnDocument.ts ID import/serialization and existing NCName character ranges at lines 74-103
- src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:120-132 and generated/internal IDs
- src/core/BpmnValidator.ts syntax/reference indexing
- src/server/tools.ts `bpmnId` versus generic `identifier`
- DI IDs, lanes, connections, root definitions, and event-definition IDs

## Implementation direction
Create one XML-1.0 NCName predicate (without a QName colon) and apply it to every semantic and DI ID at document ingress, public creation, generated-ID assertion, and validation. Include path/type in errors. Do not silently sanitize imported IDs because that can break references; reject or implement an explicit whole-document migration.

## Verification
Build a table from NCName boundaries: colon, spaces, leading digits/dash/dot, empty, combining marks, valid non-ASCII starts, supplementary code points, and malformed surrogates. Cover every ID-bearing document collection and DI reference, mutation rollback, import/export/reopen, and downstream moddle/tool interoperability.
acceptance_criteria: Every authored or imported semantic/DI ID satisfies XML Schema NCName and is unique before serialization; invalid IDs such as a:b reject with a stable path-aware error and no mutation; valid Unicode NCNames round-trip; validation flags legacy invalid files rather than declaring them syntax-valid.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: enforced XML 1.0 NCName and uniqueness across authored/imported semantic and DI IDs, added stable validation and Unicode round-trip support, and passed npm run test:all

title: Upgrade implicit Mermaid endpoints when a later explicit node declaration appears
description:
## What / impact
Mermaid edges may introduce nodes before their explicit declaration. `MermaidParser.addNode` stores the first implicit placeholder and, when it later sees the explicit declaration, emits `DUPLICATE_NODE` without replacing or merging the node. The converter therefore loses the user's label and shape and may map the wrong BPMN type.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Parse `flowchart TD\n  A --> B((End))\n  A[Actual label]`.
2. Inspect node A and parser warnings.
3. Observe the implicit label/type remain and the first explicit declaration is reported as a duplicate.

## Evidence
For `flowchart TD; A --> B((End)); A[Actual label]`, node A remained `{ id:'A', type:'process', label:'A' }` and diagnostics included `DUPLICATE_NODE`. Mermaid's normal declaration order should make A an explicitly labeled task, not an unnamed implicit placeholder.

## Where
- src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:243-307 and 431-453
- src/converters/ASTTypes.ts / MermaidConverter.ts node mapping
- tests/unit/converters and tests/integration/mermaid-conversion-edge-cases.test.ts

## Implementation direction
Track whether each stored node is implicit or explicit. On the first later explicit declaration, replace/merge the placeholder and update its source location while preserving edge/subgraph references. Warn only when a node already has an explicit definition; define deterministic handling for conflicting repeated declarations.

## Verification
Add declaration-order permutations for every supported Mermaid shape, labels/classes/subgraphs, and genuine duplicate explicit declarations. Assert AST values, warning codes/locations, BPMN types/names, node counts, and stable round-trip XML.
acceptance_criteria: A later explicit declaration supplies the node label, shape/type, class, and source location for a prior implicit edge endpoint; genuine repeated explicit declarations still produce one deterministic duplicate diagnostic; conversion output and statistics contain one node.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: implicit Mermaid endpoints upgrade in place from the first explicit declaration, with deterministic duplicate diagnostics and single-node BPMN conversion coverage

title: Fix npm test dropping configured Jest exclusions
description:
## What

The standard npm test script passes a CLI testPathIgnorePatterns value for tests/e2e. Jest replaces, rather than extends, jest.config.js testPathIgnorePatterns, so tests/integration/svg-export.test.ts runs in the source-test phase with tests/mocks/puppeteer.cjs and fails before the dedicated real-renderer phase.

## Steps to Reproduce

From the repository root, run npm test. The source Jest phase reports 1 failed suite and 2 failed SVG export tests; both receive the Puppeteer guard error. Running npm run check succeeds because its plain Jest phase honors the configured SVG exclusion and its test:renderer phase uses real Puppeteer.

## Where

package.json test and related source-test scripts; Jest configuration only if a dedicated source-test config is needed.

## Implementation

Preserve both source-phase exclusions: tests/e2e and tests/integration/svg-export.test.ts. Either use one CLI regular expression containing both paths or add a dedicated source-test Jest config. Do not add e2e to the shared jest.config.js exclusion because npm run test:all must continue exercising e2e after a clean build. Keep npm run test:renderer as the owner of the real SVG renderer suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

npm test passes; its source Jest phase excludes both e2e and svg-export.test.ts; its renderer phase executes svg-export.test.ts with real Puppeteer; npm run test:all still builds and runs e2e plus the dedicated renderer suite.

## Verification

Run npm test. Inspect the suite summaries to confirm svg-export.test.ts appears only under test:renderer. Run npm run clean and confirm dist is absent, then run npm run test:all and confirm tests/e2e/server.test.ts and the two SVG renderer tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes without running the SVG suite under the Puppeteer guard mock; source tests exclude e2e and SVG export; the renderer phase runs SVG export; npm run test:all still covers e2e and renderer tests.
close_reason: Fixed Jest source-test exclusion override and verified source, renderer, e2e, and clean aggregate test ownership

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Root cause fixed in package.json: Jest CLI testPathIgnorePatterns replaces the configured array, so the source-phase scripts now pass one alternation preserving both the e2e and SVG renderer exclusions. Evidence: source --listTests selects neither excluded path; the renderer config selects svg-export.test.ts; npm test passes 31 source suites and 526 tests, then 2 renderer tests; clean npm run check passes 32 suites and 532 tests including e2e, then 2 renderer tests.

title: Preserve underscored process IDs in listDiagrams metadata
description:

title: Choose portable BPMN versus an executable vendor extension dialect
description:
## Context
The API advertises assignee, candidate groups, and due dates while documentation claims generic BPMN compliance. These require a named extension dialect/version or a portable metadata policy.

## Where
- src/server/tools.ts activity/update schemas
- serializer/import model
- README.md and IMPLEMENTATION.md
- target engine/modeler tests

## Decision
Select and document one supported option using the criteria below.

## Rationale
Record evidence for the selected option, rejected options, compatibility impact, and follow-up dependencies.

## Alternatives Considered
- Portable BPMN core plus preserved opaque extensions.
- Camunda 7 profile.
- Camunda 8/Zeebe profile.
- Flowable/Activiti profile.
- Multi-profile API only if maintenance cost is justified.

## Decision Criteria
- Target parser/modeler interoperability.
- Namespace/version stability and typed API ergonomics.
- Portable-mode behavior and unknown-extension preservation.
- No arbitrary XML namespace/attribute injection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Decision names profile(s), namespace URIs, versions, typed fields, and compatibility guarantees.
- Portable behavior and unknown imported extension handling are explicit.
- Property feature beads depend on this decision.

## Verification
- Generate representative user tasks for shortlisted profiles and import into target modeler/parser.
- Record exact versions and fixture outcomes in decision notes.
design: Selected portable as the default document profile and camunda7 as the only opt-in executable-extension profile. Camunda 7 namespace: http://camunda.org/schema/1.0/bpmn. Tested contract: bpmn-moddle 9.0.2 plus camunda-bpmn-moddle 7.0.1. Allowlisted UserTask fields for mcp-bpmn-g7s: assignee string, candidateGroups string array serialized comma-separated, and dueDate string; update null removes a field. Portable mode rejects these fields and emits no vendor namespace. Unknown warning-free imported extensions remain opaque and are semantically retained; arbitrary namespace, QName, attribute, and raw XML authoring are forbidden. Profile selection applies to all authored creation paths, open_bpmn detects actual namespace use with descriptor reparse, and current plus creation/open results report extensionProfile. Parser compatibility is guaranteed only for the exact tested versions, not Camunda deployment, execution, rendering, or modeler releases.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision names profile(s), namespace URIs, versions, typed fields, and compatibility guarantees.
- Portable behavior and unknown imported extension handling are explicit.
- Property feature beads depend on this decision.
notes: Verification on 2026-08-22 with Node 25.9.0: portable-user-task.bpmn parsed humanPerformer and potentialOwner with zero bpmn-moddle 9.0.2 warnings and retained exact types/expressions through descriptor round-trip and unrelated MCP-BPMN mutation. camunda7-user-task.bpmn parsed assignee, candidateGroups, and dueDate with zero warnings using bpmn-moddle 9.0.2 plus camunda-bpmn-moddle 7.0.1; all fields survived descriptor round-trip and unrelated MCP-BPMN mutation. Core moddle also retained the Camunda attributes opaquely in $attrs. npx jest tests/integration/dialect-compatibility.test.ts --runInBand passed 5/5. npm run test:all passed 28 suites, 445 tests, with 5 existing todos. npm run lint and npm run type-check passed. mcp-bpmn-g7s directly depends on this decision. ADR: docs/decisions/0001-bpmn-extension-profile.md.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: selected portable default plus typed Camunda 7 profile, documented compatibility and opaque-extension policy, added exact-version parser fixtures/tests, and confirmed the property bead dependency.

title: Mermaid edge IDs collide when multiple edges connect the same two nodes
description:
## What
Parallel Mermaid edges with the same endpoints receive duplicate AST IDs such as A_to_B. The AST array retains both and current BPMN generation assigns fresh Flow_N IDs, so there is no current overwrite/data loss; the defect violates stable unique AST identity and can break future keyed consumers.

## Steps to Reproduce
