title: auto_layout has no scopeId: one subprocess or pool cannot be laid out in isolation
description:
## Context

mcp-bpmn-9sv.16 delivered spacing and pinnedElementIds. scopeId, the third option it named, was attempted and deliberately left out.

## Why it was not done

bpmn-auto-layout returns a whole ranked plane. Merging one scope's block back into the live plane needs the containing subprocess or pool grown around the result, and the out-of-scope siblings the grown container then runs into could not be made oracle-clean in the general case. A merge that leaves overlapping siblings is worse than no option at all.

## What it needs first

A decision about what a scoped layout is allowed to move outside its scope: nothing at all (and fail when the result does not fit), the containing scope only, or the whole plane below and right of it. Each gives a different, defensible tool. pinnedElementIds is the natural building block for the first of them.
close_reason: scopeId lays out one expanded subprocess or one pool in isolation (option 2: the containing scope only). New src/core/layout/ScopedLayout.ts merges the ranked block for the named scope back into the live plane - everything outside the scope is restored to the geometry it had, the container keeps the size the ranking gave it (a caller-chosen size stays a floor), and the siblings that box now runs into are pushed right or down by exactly one 20px clearance as rigid bodies, cascading up through each containing subprocess/pool. Connections are re-routed only where geometry actually changed, and the pass refuses (ScopedLayoutError, nothing committed) rather than commit an overlap or a containment break. scopeId rejects anything but an expanded subprocess/transaction or a white-box pool, refuses a subprocess inside a laned process, and cannot be combined with pinnedElementIds. Pinned by tests/integration/layout-scope.test.ts (9 cases, all fail before / pass after, each asserting validateBpmnGeometry has no diagnostics); layout, geometry and collaboration suites plus the full 57-suite run stay green. scopeId is on AutoLayoutOptions and awaits wiring in src/server/tools.ts by the tool-boundary owner.

title: One unsupported Mermaid shape cascades into three errors about a different, correctly written node
description:
## Evidence

Found by driving the built server over stdio as an agent.

    flowchart TD
      subgraph cust ["Customer"]
        A([Start]) --> B[Place order]
      end
      subgraph shop ["Shop"]
        C[Receive] --> D((Done))
      end
      B --> C

reports four errors:

    1:1 [MISSING_START]           No explicit start node found
    3:6 [UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE]       stadium shape "([...])" on node "A" ...
    8:3 [MISSING_SUBGRAPH_OWNER]  Mermaid node B is not owned by a subgraph
    8:3 [DISCONNECTED_NODE]       Node "B" has no incoming connections

Only the second is real. B is declared inside subgraph cust on line 3 and has an incoming edge from A. Because line 3 fails on A's shape, B loses its declaration and its subgraph membership, so the later reference on line 8 registers it fresh and outside any subgraph, and the connectivity and ownership analyses then both report it.

The agent is pointed at line 8 twice for a problem whose entire fix is one character on line 3, and A([Start]) is the most common way to write a start node in Mermaid, so this is a likely first encounter with the tool.

## Related

mcp-bpmn-j21.7 fixed exactly this shape for malformed subgraph declarations, by pushing a placeholder so the follow-on analyses stay quiet. The same treatment is needed for a node whose declaring line failed.

## Fix

When a line fails to parse, still register the endpoints that parsed successfully, with their subgraph membership, so downstream ownership and connectivity checks see the author's intent. Failing that, suppress ownership and connectivity diagnostics for any node whose declaration site reported an error. Pin it with a test asserting this input yields exactly one error.
close_reason: MermaidParser now withholds every whole-graph analysis (MISSING_SUBGRAPH_OWNER, MISSING_START/END, DISCONNECTED_NODE, IMPLICIT_PARALLEL_SPLIT) when a line failed to parse, since the graph those analyses read is missing whatever that line declared. Faults computed from content that did parse (DUPLICATE_SUBGRAPH, MULTIPLE_SUBGRAPH_OWNERS, UNSUPPORTED_EDGE_ENDPOINT, edge-style warnings) still report. The bead's example now yields exactly one error and no warnings. Pinned by the four cases in 'MermaidParser diagnostics after a failed line (mcp-bpmn-j21.13)' in tests/unit/converters/MermaidParser.test.ts; three fail before the change and the control case ('runs every analysis once the whole document parses') passes both sides.

title: Element ids continue across new_bpmn, so the first task in a fresh diagram is Task_4
description:
## Evidence

Found by driving the built server over stdio as an agent.

After working on one diagram, new_bpmn then add_activity returns:

    {"elementId": "Task_4", "elementType": "bpmn:Task"}

list_elements on the new, otherwise empty diagram confirms only Task_4 and Task_5 exist. IdGenerator.reset() is called only from SimpleBpmnEngine.clear(), which new_bpmn does not go through, so the counter runs for the life of the process.

## Impact

Two consequences, the second worse than the first.

The papercut: an agent that writes attachTo: "Task_1" against a diagram it just created gets "Boundary events require attachTo referencing an existing activity". Recoverable, since the create call returns the real id, but it costs a round trip and the message does not say which id was missing.

The real one: the same modelling steps produce different ids depending on what the session did beforehand. Two runs of the same agent script generate diagrams that differ throughout, so the output is not reproducible and does not diff cleanly. For a tool whose product is a file people review in version control, that matters.

## Fix

Reset the counter when a diagram becomes the current context through new_bpmn and new_from_mermaid. Opening an existing file must not reset, since its ids are already allocated and the generator has to avoid colliding with them. Pin it: create, add a task, create again, add a task, assert both are Task_1.
close_reason: createProcess resets the element counters, so a diagram created from scratch numbers from one and the same modelling steps produce the same ids. Root counters keep running deliberately: two engines in one process can hold diagrams at once and a reused Process id would make their contexts indistinguishable, which the concurrent-creation persistence test proves. Pinned by 'numbers a new diagram from one instead of continuing the previous one'.

title: Every mutation response repeats the filename and two 74-character revision tokens
description:
## Evidence

Measured across 35 tool responses from a real modelling session:

    structuredContent total                          36,106 bytes
    filename / revision / previousFilename fields      5,696 bytes (15%)
    average per response                              162 bytes of the 1,031

A revision token is 74 characters (sha256:<64 hex>:vN) and mutations carry two of them, before and after. Until save_as is called the filename is a 112-character generated placeholder, repeated in full on every single response:

    mcp-bpmn-v1_WyJDb2xsYWJvcmF0aW9uXzEiLCJPcmRlciBIYW5kbGluZyIsIjc5YTAzMGNkMmZjNzRiMTk5MDM5ODkzOGEzMjM2OWY5Il0.bpmn

## Impact

15% of every mutation result is context the agent almost never reads. beforeRevision is knowable — it is the afterRevision of the previous call — and the filename does not change between calls. On a 40-call modelling session this is a few thousand tokens of pure repetition.

## Fix

Options, cheapest first: shorten the revision token to a truncated digest plus the version counter, which is all the compare-and-set needs; drop beforeRevision, since a caller that wants it already has it; and return the filename only when it changes, the way previousFilename and removedPreviousFile already work. Any of these is a contract change, so it belongs with the response-shape work in mcp-bpmn-8u0.25 rather than on its own.
close_reason: Revision tokens are halved: the digest is truncated to 128 bits, which is ample for the equality comparison a compare-and-set needs, taking each token from 74 to 42 characters and each mutation result from two 74-character tokens to two 42s. Deliberately did not do the other two parts: dropping beforeRevision removes information a caller uses to describe what it changed, and shortening the generated placeholder filename would break the metadata that list_diagrams reads out of it without opening files, which contract test G6 pins. Both are recorded here rather than done blind.

title: open_bpmn's elementCount and list_elements' count disagree with no explanation
description:
## Evidence

Found by driving the built server over stdio as an agent.

Reopening a saved collaboration:

    open_bpmn    -> elementCount: 16, connectionCount: 13
    list_elements -> count: 20  (14 flowNode, 3 lane, 2 participant, 1 association)

elementCount counts flow nodes and participants only. Lanes and associations are elements to list_elements but not to elementCount, and an association is not a connection either, so it appears in neither headline number.

## Impact

An agent that opens a file, reads "16 elements", then lists and receives 20 has to work out which definition each number uses. current and new_bpmn report the same field, so the mismatch shows up on every entry into a diagram.

## Fix

Either make elementCount agree with list_elements' count, or name the fields for what they measure and say so in both tool descriptions.
close_reason: open_bpmn now reports laneCount alongside elementCount and connectionCount, and both its description and its text say what each number measures and why list_elements returns a larger total. Chose to name the measurements rather than redefine elementCount, which is load-bearing in the e2e and contract suites.

title: Mermaid steering conventions for gateway, task and event subtypes
description:
## Context

mcp-bpmn-j21.11 delivered the preview half: preview_mermaid converts Mermaid text and reports the elements, connections and pools it would create, with no file or context effect. The second half of that issue, conventions that let an author steer the mapping, was not delivered.

## Missing

There is no way to ask for a parallel rather than exclusive gateway, a user or service task rather than a plain task, or a typed event, from Mermaid text. An author sees what they will get from preview_mermaid but still cannot change it without switching to the typed tools.

## Fix

Add conventions to the supported subset and the parser, for example a distinct gateway shape for a parallel split and a class suffix for task and event subtypes. Document them in the skill capabilities reference and in preview_mermaid's description, and keep preview_mermaid reporting the resulting types so an author can check the steering worked.
close_reason: Added Mermaid ':::class' subtype steering: seven task classes (user/service/script/businessRule/manual/receive/send), four gateway classes (parallel/inclusive/eventBased/complex), nine event-definition classes (message/timer/error/signal/conditional/escalation/compensation/cancel/terminate), plus :::task and :::exclusive as neutral spellings of the defaults. Names match ignoring case, '-' and '_'. Vocabulary and BPMN legality table live in src/converters/ASTTypes.ts; MermaidParser resolves annotations after type inference and reports INVALID_NODE_SUBTYPE at the ':::' when a class is illegal on its node or conflicts with another on the same node; SimpleBpmnGenerator maps subtypes to BPMN types and emits eventDefinition properties, choosing IntermediateCatchEvent over ThrowEvent per definition. classDef/class directives stay ignored-with-warning; unknown classes stay ignored-with-warning. Documented in skills/bpmn-modeler/references/capabilities.md. Pinned by 'MermaidParser BPMN subtype classes (mcp-bpmn-j21.12)' (35 cases) in tests/unit/converters/MermaidParser.test.ts, 'SimpleBpmnGenerator subtype steering (mcp-bpmn-j21.12)' (28 cases) in tests/unit/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.test.ts and 'converts a fully steered diagram to valid BPMN (mcp-bpmn-j21.12)' in tests/integration/mermaid-conversion.test.ts, which also asserts BpmnValidator reports valid at full level. preview_mermaid's description in src/server/tools.ts still needs the new wording (reported to the caller; that file is not mine).

title: FileManager.validatePath, listBpmnFiles and getFileInfo have no production caller
description:
## Context

mcp-bpmn-iqa.11 cleared the build and config leftovers but left three FileManager methods in place.

## Evidence

validatePath, listBpmnFiles and getFileInfo have no caller under src/. Their only consumers are tests, but those tests are not dead: validatePath sits inside the security case 'uses separator-aware containment and rejects the directory-capable sibling escape', and the other two sit beside live saveBpmnFile/readBpmnFile assertions.

## Why it needs its own change

Removing them means rewriting working security tests rather than deleting dead ones, and jest.config.js enforces a 70/60/70/70 coverage floor on FileManager that dropping fully covered code would move.

## Fix

Either give the security assertions a path through the live API and delete the three helpers, or document them as a deliberately kept test seam.
close_reason: Deleted FileManager.validatePath, listBpmnFiles and getFileInfo, none of which had a caller under src/ (listing is SimpleBpmnEngine.listDiagrams, containment is SafeFilePath.isPathContained, metadata is fs.stat). The security case 'uses separator-aware containment and rejects the directory-capable sibling escape' in tests/unit/utils/FileSecurity.test.ts now asserts isPathContained, the production predicate validatePath merely wrapped, beside its unchanged live saveBpmnFile assertion. Pinned by 'keeps the workspace boundary separator-aware through the live save API', 'saves and reads back exactly the bytes it wrote inside its unique temporary root' and 'creates a missing workspace on first save and leaves unrelated files alone' in tests/unit/utils/FileManager.test.ts. FileManager coverage 83.78/65.11/88.23/83.78, above the 70/60/70/70 floor.

title: Decide the fate of MermaidConverter.canConvert and analyze
description:
## Context

mcp-bpmn-iqa.8 removed the phantom parts of the Mermaid converter surface but left canConvert and analyze in place. Neither has a production caller: preview_mermaid, added in mcp-bpmn-j21.11, builds its own summary from convert output rather than calling either.

## Why it was left

They are exercised by 34 assertions across tests/unit/converters/MermaidConverter.test.ts and tests/integration/mermaid-conversion.test.ts, whose design is that all three entry points report the same diagnostics. Deleting them means rewriting those suites, not deleting dead tests.

## Fix

Pick one, deliberately, in a single change: either have preview_mermaid report the analysis so both become production-reachable, or delete both and reduce the consistency assertions to convert alone.
close_reason: Deleted MermaidConverter.canConvert, analyze, their ValidationResult/AnalysisResult shapes and the calculateComplexity/identifySupportedFeatures/identifyUnsupportedFeatures helpers, plus the equally caller-less ConversionOptions.validateOutput; repo-wide grep found callers only in tests. Consistency assertions in tests/unit/converters/MermaidConverter.test.ts and tests/integration/mermaid-conversion.test.ts now run through convert alone: the analyze node census became a BPMN element-type census over convert output, canConvert's supportedFeatures assertions became assertions on the emitted elements and flows. Pinned by 'MermaidConverter node census', 'retains labeled-flow support after parser validation' and 'emits the start and end events the diagram declares' in tests/unit/converters/MermaidConverter.test.ts; the pre-deletion suite fails 29/29 against the new source.

title: Validator warns about missing incoming/outgoing flows on activities inside an ad-hoc subprocess
description:
## Context

mcp-bpmn-a3j.25 stopped the executable-profile check from demanding start and end events in an ad-hoc subprocess scope, and from demanding incoming/outgoing flows on an event subprocess.

## Gap

Activities *inside* an ad-hoc subprocess still draw MISSING_INCOMING_FLOW and MISSING_OUTGOING_FLOW. Ad-hoc activities are unordered by definition, so those flows are exactly what the construct says will not exist. This is the same class of false positive, outside the fixed issue's stated scope.

## Fix

Skip the incoming/outgoing checks for flow nodes whose containing scope is a bpmn:AdHocSubProcess, with a no-false-positive twin proving an ordinary subprocess still reports them.
close_reason: The executable-profile node loop is now skipped entirely for an ad-hoc subprocess scope, reusing the existing boundedScope flag that already suppressed the start/end event warnings, so activities inside a bpmn:AdHocSubProcess no longer draw MISSING_INCOMING_FLOW/MISSING_OUTGOING_FLOW. Pinned by 'does not ask activities inside an ad-hoc subprocess for sequence flows' in tests/unit/core/BpmnValidator.test.ts (fails before, passes after); no-false-positive twin 'still asks activities inside an ordinary subprocess for sequence flows' proves a plain subprocess scope still reports both codes for a disconnected inner task.

title: get_workspace does not report a startup configuration that was refused
description:
## Context

WorkspaceSession.getStartupFailure() records why a repository .mcp-bpmn.json was ignored (bad JSON, wrong shape, dot-segment escape, symlink traversal). Today only select_workspace surfaces it, and only when the agent tries to switch.

## Gap

An operator who misconfigured the repository sees a server that silently runs in the launch directory. get_workspace, the tool whose whole job is explaining where diagrams go, says nothing about the refused configuration.

## Fix

Add an optional field to the get_workspace result carrying the refusal reason. The output schema is .strict(), so this needs the schema in tools.ts and the handler in handlers.ts together.
close_reason: WorkspaceSession.getInfo now carries startupFailure, so get_workspace reports a repository config or MCP_BPMN_DIAGRAMS_PATH that was refused at startup instead of leaving the agent to discover it by attempting a selection. Pinned by 'reports a refused startup configuration through get_workspace' and a twin asserting the field is absent when the configuration was applied.

title: Message flows traverse a foreign pool's interior instead of leaving it directly
description:
## Evidence
In the laid-out 2-pool/2-lane collaboration MessageFlow_1 runs 368px horizontally inside the Customer pool under its tasks before dropping to the other pool (src/core/layout/ConnectionRouter.ts:84-88, :586-590, :426-452).

## Fix
Add a per-unit cost for route length inside a non-owner participant so the router exits the foreign pool immediately.
close_reason: ConnectionRouter now charges FOREIGN_INTERIOR_COST_PER_UNIT for every unit a route runs inside a participant that does not own the connection, so a message flow leaves its pool instead of crossing a foreign one. Folded into the route total rather than adding a scoring field, following the dockSidePenalty precedent. Pinned by tests/unit/layout/ConnectionRouter.test.ts.

title: Duplicate bpmn-auto-layout-alpha dev alias and a 72-subprocess layout-candidate matrix run on every npm test
description:
## Evidence
package.json devDependencies bpmn-auto-layout-alpha aliases the same version as the production bpmn-auto-layout (2x2.7 MB in npm-shrinkwrap.json:2798-2870); stable/yabal are dev-only (prod uses only bpmn-auto-layout), yet tests/unit/layout/layout-candidates.test.ts:115-136, :253-262 spawns the 72-subprocess candidate matrix on every npm test (jest.config.js:30-35).

## Fix
Drop the alias; move the candidate matrix behind an opt-in script or CI-only job.
close_reason: Dropped the bpmn-auto-layout-alpha dev alias; the layout-candidate tests now import the production bpmn-auto-layout at the same version. The three dev-only comparison candidates sit behind MCP_BPMN_LAYOUT_CANDIDATES=1, which test:all sets, so npm test went from 9.5s and 73 subprocesses to 3.5s and 19 while CI still runs the full matrix. Both lockfiles were regenerated in place with npm install --package-lock-only and npm ci verified clean.

title: auto_layout bumps the revision and rewrites the file even when it produces byte-identical DI
description:
## Evidence
Running auto_layout twice yields byte-identical output, yet beforeRevision !== afterRevision every time (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2088-2120; src/server/handlers.ts:1342-1360).

## Fix
Compare the serialized output with the current document and skip the commit when unchanged; return changed:false.
close_reason: applyAutoLayout now parses the adapter result, applies the collaboration policy and any transposition, then compares a geometry signature (element/lane bounds, connection waypoints, shape isHorizontal) against the live document. An identical layout is not committed: no revision bump, no file write, and the tool returns changed:false with a message saying so. Pinned by tests/unit/core/LayoutOrientation.test.ts.

title: Missing release-grade test categories: property/fuzz tests and a large-diagram performance bound
description:
## Evidence
No fast-check or fuzzing anywhere; no performance.now / time-bound assertions (resource limits are asserted by count only in tests/security/resource-exhaustion.test.ts).

## Fix
fast-check properties for isBpmnId(sanitize(s)), Mermaid parser error typing (never throws, always typed diagnostics), and import/export idempotence; an opt-in 2,000-element benchmark with a time bound.
close_reason: Added deterministic property/fuzz suites and large-diagram bounds. tests/helpers/seededRandom.ts is a pinned-seed mulberry32 generator (no new dependency); tests/property/mermaid-parser.property.test.ts (seed 0x5e7130) fuzzes 400 inputs through MermaidParser.parse for typed diagnostics, unique edge IDs and determinism, plus 500 FileManager.sanitizeFilename cases; tests/property/bpmn-import.property.test.ts (seed 0x5e7131) drives MermaidConverter.convert and SimpleBpmnEngine.importXml/exportXml for NCName-valid IDs, import/export idempotence and 120 mutated-XML cases, all inside a temp dir. tests/performance/large-diagram.performance.test.ts bounds work always-on (500 nodes: 500 elements, 548 flows, 490.5 bytes/element vs a 800 ceiling; byte growth 2.01x on doubling vs a 2.4 ceiling) and gates the 2,000-element benchmark behind MCP_BPMN_PERF=1 via npm run test:performance (measured 414 ms idle / 890 ms under load, budget 8 s). Verified teeth: the parser property suite fails with 'duplicate edge IDs' when the j21.9 fix is reverted.

title: tests/README.md describes a test tree that no longer exists
description:
## Evidence
tests/README.md:5-17 lists only unit/utils/, says "Core component tests would go here"; omits security/contracts/e2e/helpers, test:renderer, test:e2e:compiled, and the Chrome requirement.

## Fix
Regenerate from the tree; link the CONTRIBUTING table.
close_reason: Rewrote tests/README.md from the real tree: a table for unit/integration/contracts/security/property/performance/e2e/helpers/fixtures/mocks plus the top-level installer shell suite, the jest testMatch, the two excluded paths (test:e2e:compiled after a build, test:renderer under jest.puppeteer.config.js with the Chrome requirement), the MCP_BPMN_LAYOUT_CANDIDATES and MCP_BPMN_PERF opt-in gates, test:evaluations, the property/fuzz conventions, and a link to the CONTRIBUTING command table instead of a duplicate. Pinned by the new tests/integration/test-suite-documentation.test.ts, which fails 5 of 6 cases against the previous README (missing contracts/e2e/helpers/performance/property/security, both env gates, test:renderer/test:e2e:compiled/test:contract/test:evaluations/test:performance, the CONTRIBUTING link, and the 'would go here' placeholder).

title: Two identical 289 KB lockfiles with no check that they stay identical
description:
## Evidence
package-lock.json and npm-shrinkwrap.json are byte-identical today; npm prefers and auto-packs shrinkwrap (listing it in files, package.json:17, is redundant); scripts/package-smoke.mjs:496 checks only shrinkwrap root deps vs package.json; CI caches on package-lock (.github/workflows/ci.yml:30-31); the SessionStart hook's npm install rewrites shrinkwrap and would leave package-lock behind on drift.

## Fix
Keep one lockfile and generate shrinkwrap in prepack, or add a cmp check to the smoke test; document in CONTRIBUTING.
close_reason: scripts/package-smoke.mjs now byte-compares package-lock.json and npm-shrinkwrap.json and fails with the safe repair (npm install, never delete-and-reinstall). CONTRIBUTING.md documents why there are two lockfiles and the two regressions that came from regenerating them the wrong way.

title: ralph-loop/tests/loop_test.sh is never run by any script or workflow
description:
## Evidence
grep for ralph / loop_test across package.json, Makefile and .github/workflows finds nothing.

## Fix
Add test:ralph to test:all, or delete the loop and its tests if they are not part of the product.
close_reason: Added the test:ralph script and appended it to test:all, so ralph-loop/tests/loop_test.sh runs in CI. Added a jq/perl/git prerequisite guard so a missing tool fails clearly. The suite is hermetic: it builds temp fixtures with fake bd, codex and claude on PATH.

title: Dead code and stale build/config leftovers (unused FileManager/IdGenerator exports, barrels, .node-options, build.js, jest ignore for a deleted file)
description:
## Evidence
src/utils/FileManager.ts:79-101, :105-110, :294-331 (generateDefaultFilename/validatePath/getFileInfo/listBpmnFiles), src/utils/IdGenerator.ts:35-56 (generateElementId), src/server/tools.ts DEFAULT_PAGE_LIMIT, src/config/index.ts:56, :80 have no consumer in src/ (tests only); src/core/layout/index.ts and adapters/index.ts barrels are unreachable from the entry; jest.config.js:38 ignores coverage for the non-existent AutoLayoutEnhanced.ts; .node-options is read by nothing; build-cjs.js:19-21 targets node18 vs engines >=22.12 and externalizes non-dependency jsdom; build.js is referenced nowhere; FileManager.ts:48 comment still says ~/mcp-bpmn.

## Fix
Delete the unused exports/barrels/files, fix the jest ignore, set the bundle target to node22, drop the jsdom external.
close_reason: Deleted build.js and .node-options, retargeted build-cjs.js from node18 to node22 and dropped its jsdom external (jsdom is in neither dependency list and imported nowhere), and removed IdGenerator.generateElementId, a stale duplicate of the live prefixing path that had already drifted by missing bpmn:Association. Both layout barrels and the AutoLayoutEnhanced coverage ignore were already gone. Two claims in the issue were wrong and were left alone with evidence: FileManager.generateDefaultFilename has a live caller, and the ~/mcp-bpmn comment is accurate. The three remaining FileManager helpers are tracked in mcp-bpmn-iqa.13.

comments.author: Claude

PARTIALLY DONE (left open deliberately - remaining items are in files owned by other agents this session).

title: Filename validation accepts Windows reserved device names and Unicode bidi/control characters
description:
## Evidence
src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts:665-706 assertSafeFilename accepts CON.bpmn, aux.bpmn, com1.bpmn, foo..bpmn, a name containing U+202E, and a lone combining mark. WSL2 (/mnt/c) is a supported platform (README.md:28-30).

## Fix
Reject ^(CON|PRN|AUX|NUL|COM[1-9]|LPT[1-9])(\.|$)/i and C0/C1 + \p{Cf} characters.
close_reason: assertSafeFilename in src/utils/SafeFilePath.ts now rejects Windows reserved device names (CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-9/LPT1-9, with or without an extension and ignoring trailing spaces/dots) and any C0/DEL/C1 control or Unicode format character (bidi overrides, isolates, marks, ZWJ, soft hyphen). Pinned by tests/unit/utils/SafeFilePath.test.ts 'assertSafeFilename hostile names', whose twin asserts 20 ordinary names including console.bpmn, com10.bpmn and the 200-byte non-ASCII name are still accepted.

title: A malformed .mcp-bpmn.json crashes the server at import time instead of reporting through MCP
description:
## Evidence
src/server/index.ts:51 WorkspaceSession.fromLaunch() runs at module top level outside main().catch (src/config/WorkspaceSession.ts:53-56, :122-124). Probe with `{not json`: exit 1 with a stack trace on stderr before initialize.

## Fix
Resolve the workspace inside main() through the shutdown('startup failure', 1) path with a one-line message, or fall back to launch_cwd with a warning exposed via get_workspace.
close_reason: WorkspaceSession.fromLaunch no longer throws when .mcp-bpmn.json cannot be applied: it degrades to the launch cwd, records the reason (getStartupFailure()), and resolveSelection/activateSelection raise it so it reaches the client as a select_workspace tool error. Pinned by tests/unit/config/WorkspaceSession.test.ts 'an unusable .mcp-bpmn.json', including the tool-error case; verified end to end that initialize now answers instead of the process dying.

title: Remove bpmn-js upstream files copied into docs/ (SETUP.md, setup scripts, translations.json)
description:
## Evidence
docs/project/SETUP.md describes setting up a bpmn-js dev environment; docs/project/setup.sh, setup-alternative.sh, setup.bat clone bpmn-io/{diagram-js,bpmn-js,bpmn-moddle}; docs/translations.json is the bpmn-js UI string list. No references outside docs/project.

## Fix
Delete docs/project/ and docs/translations.json.
close_reason: git rm docs/project/ (SETUP.md, setup.sh, setup-alternative.sh, setup.bat) and docs/translations.json. All are verbatim bpmn-js upstream files: SETUP.md documents cloning bpmn-io/{bpmn-js,diagram-js,bpmn-moddle} and the scripts do that cloning; translations.json is the bpmn-js UI string list. The only reference anywhere was SETUP.md linking its own sibling scripts. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md attribution covers the bpmn-js dependency itself and does not depend on these copied files.

title: Document Puppeteer's 650 MB Chrome download and the installer's reliance on the checkout cache
description:
## Evidence
~/.cache/puppeteer is 652 MB after npm ci. README.md:35-46 never names PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD, the size, or the network requirement. scripts/install-agent-integrations.sh:890-893 installs with PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=true, so the installed server only renders because the checkout's npm ci filled the shared cache (or a system Chrome exists).

## Fix
Add a "Browser download" paragraph: size, PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 for XML-only use, PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH, and that make install does not download a browser.
close_reason: README gained a Browser download section: the measured 652 MB Puppeteer cache, PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD and PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH, and the fact that make install never downloads so it relies on the shared cache, a system Chrome, or the env var. Cross-referenced from CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: Delete stray root-level debug scripts that target a tool API that no longer exists
description:
## Evidence
debug-moddle.cjs, test-bpmn-moddle.cjs:7,42-91, test-mcp-server.js:62-84 call bpmn_create_process, bpmn_add_event (with processId), bpmn_get_diagrams_path, bpmn_list_diagrams (none exist) and spawn dist/server/bundle.cjs (not produced by npm run build). Referenced by nothing; linted by npm run lint.

## Fix
git rm all three.
close_reason: git rm debug-moddle.cjs, test-bpmn-moddle.cjs and test-mcp-server.js. Repo-wide grep (excluding node_modules/.git/dist/coverage) found no reference to any of the three outside the bead text itself; none appear in package.json files/scripts, the Makefile, scripts/, bin/, or .github/workflows/ci.yml. They were only being linted by 'npm run lint', which lints '.' for .ts/.js/.cjs/.mjs.

title: IMPLEMENTATION.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the README env-var list describe a previous version
description:
## Evidence
IMPLEMENTATION.md:60-92 tool table lists 28 of 39 tools; :126-128 "Diagram storage defaults to ~/mcp-bpmn" and CONTRIBUTING.md:78-80 "the normal ~/mcp-bpmn diagram directory" contradict WorkspaceSession.fromLaunch(); IMPLEMENTATION.md:245-247 "Mermaid conversion uses LayoutEngine" (file deleted); MCP_BPMN_MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES (src/config/index.ts:110) is absent from both env lists and README.md:848-855 also omits MCP_BPMN_MAX_IMPORT_ELEMENTS/_FLOWS/_DI_ELEMENTS; README.md:901-905 project structure puts layout in src/utils.

## Fix
Regenerate the tool table from toolDefinitions, fix the storage statements, delete the LayoutEngine sentence, list every MCP_BPMN_* variable.
close_reason: Removed the false LayoutEngine claim from IMPLEMENTATION.md, replaced the '~/mcp-bpmn' default with the real three-step workspace resolution in IMPLEMENTATION.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, and rebuilt the README env table from src/config with all 16 variables, their effect and default. Project structure and Key Components now match the tree on disk.

title: README performance/tarball numbers are stale by ~2x
description:
## Evidence
README.md:928-940 claims 195 kB packed / 1,104,270 bytes unpacked. `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts` today: 336.7 kB packed / 2.0 MB unpacked / 137 files (60 .map files; tools.d.ts alone is 229.7 kB).

## Fix
Refresh or drop the numbers; consider excluding *.map and *.d.ts from files for a CLI-only package.
close_reason: README's tarball figures were remeasured with npm pack --dry-run --json: 357,920 B packed, 2,079,332 B unpacked, 141 files, with the composition breakdown that explains the size. The stale 195 kB / 1,104,270 B numbers are gone.

title: README documents the wrong default diagram filename format
description:
## Evidence
README.md:968 (and :868-869): "New diagrams start with the filename {ProcessId}_{ProcessName}.bpmn". Actual (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2822-2834): `mcp-bpmn-v1_<base64url([id,name,uuid])>.bpmn`; the {id}_{name}_{uuid} form is only the >200-byte fallback.

## Fix
Document the real scheme, or implement the readable default proposed in the filename bead and update the README then.
close_reason: README gained a Diagram filenames section written from the code: the placeholder is mcp-bpmn-v1_<base64url([id,name,uuid])>.bpmn, the {id}_{name}_{uuid} form is only the over-200-byte fallback, and save_as deletes a placeholder but never a chosen name. The optional filename arguments on new_bpmn, new_from_mermaid and open_mermaid_file are documented in each tool's section.

title: new_bpmn / open_* / delete_diagram_file do not say in their text that they replaced or closed the active diagram
description:
## Evidence
delete_diagram_file on the active file -> closedCurrent:true in structuredContent but the text is only `Deleted diagram file: approval.bpmn`; the description (src/server/tools.ts:1578) omits the side effect. new_bpmn while another diagram is current -> `Created new process diagram "Second"` with no mention that the previous one was replaced (src/server/handlers.ts:1396-1410, :407-420).

## Fix
Mention it in the descriptions; append "(closed the active diagram)" / "(replaced active diagram X)" in the text.
close_reason: new_bpmn/new_from_mermaid/open_bpmn/open_mermaid_file now append '(replaced and closed the previously active diagram "X" in file)' to their text and report an optional replacedDiagram in structuredContent (replaceCurrent returns the displaced diagram); delete_diagram_file appends '(closed the active diagram; there is no current diagram now)' when closedCurrent; all five tool descriptions state the side effect. Pinned by tests/integration/handlers.test.ts 'names the diagram it replaced or closed' (fails before) plus 'says nothing about a replacement when no diagram was open'.

title: Zod regex failures surface as a bare 'Invalid' (expectedRevision, geometry revisions)
description:
## Evidence
`add_gateway {…, expectedRevision:"nope"}` -> `Invalid arguments for tool "add_gateway": expectedRevision: Invalid` (src/server/tools.ts:91-94, :1650-1655).

## Fix
Add messages to the .regex() calls (revision, outputGeometryRevision) describing the expected format.
close_reason: Added explanatory messages to every revision-token .regex() in src/server/tools.ts (document revision, outputGeometryRevision, outputSemanticRevision, geometryPatchConnectionUpdate.expectedGeometryRevision), so a bad expectedRevision now reports 'Document revision must be a token returned by a prior result, of the form "sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters>:v<number>"' instead of a bare 'Invalid'. Pinned by tests/security/request-validation.test.ts 'names the expected revision-token format instead of a bare "Invalid"' (fails before: all four cases reported ': Invalid').

title: get_diagrams_path tells the agent to set an environment variable instead of pointing at select_workspace
description:
## Evidence
src/server/handlers.ts:1415-1416 response text: "…You can set a custom path using the environment variable: MCP_BPMN_DIAGRAMS_PATH".

## Fix
Point to select_workspace / get_workspace.
close_reason: get_diagrams_path text now points at get_workspace/select_workspace instead of telling the agent to set MCP_BPMN_DIAGRAMS_PATH (src/server/handlers.ts getDiagramsPath). Pinned by tests/integration/handlers.test.ts 'should return the exact isolated diagrams path', whose existing assertion encoded the old env-var wording and was updated deliberately; it also asserts the text no longer mentions MCP_BPMN_DIAGRAMS_PATH (fails before).

title: list_elements rows carry kind only for associations
description:
## Evidence
Rows show kind:"association" for associations but no kind for participants, lanes, flow nodes, or artifacts (laneQueryView sets kind:'lane' but the row mapper at src/server/handlers.ts:879-895 omits it; :1487-1496).

## Fix
Emit kind (flowNode|artifact|participant|lane|association) on every row.
close_reason: list_elements rows now carry kind (flowNode|artifact|participant|lane|association) for every row instead of associations only, get_element details carry it too, and outputQueryBase.kind became a required z.enum (src/server/handlers.ts listElements/getElement, src/server/tools.ts). Pinned by tests/integration/handlers.test.ts 'labels every listed row with its kind, not only associations' (fails before: 6 rows had no kind).

title: Owner/scope errors should say which ID to pass (pool vs processId vs scopeId)
description:
## Evidence
`add_activity {ownerId:"Participant_1"}` -> `Missing BPMN process owner: Participant_1` (needs Participant_1_Process); `add_activity {ownerId:"SubProcess_1"}` -> same message (needs scopeId); `add_lane {poolId:"Participant_2_Process"}` -> `Participant Participant_2_Process not found` (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:3043, :786).

## Fix
Detect and hint: "Participant_1 is a pool; pass its processId Participant_1_Process as ownerId" / "SubProcess_1 is a subprocess; pass it as scopeId" / "add_lane takes the pool elementId".
close_reason: Owner/scope rejections now name the id to pass: SimpleBpmnEngine.assertFlowScope appends ownerHint/scopeHint ('Participant_1 is a pool; pass its process id Participant_1_Process as ownerId.', 'SubProcess_1 is a bpmn:SubProcess; pass P as ownerId and SubProcess_1 as scopeId.', pool-as-scopeId, wrong-owner scope, and a list of valid process ids), and addLane appends poolHint ('X is a process id; add_lane takes the pool elementId, which is Participant_1.'). handlers.ts gained a '^Participant X not found' classifier so that case now reports owner_or_scope_invalid with a poolId detail instead of unexpected_error. Pinned by tests/integration/handlers.test.ts 'names the id to pass for pools, processes, and subprocesses' (fails before).

title: route_connection is annotated destructive although its default mode is proposal-only
description:
## Evidence
src/server/tools.ts:1453 annotations: DESTRUCTIVE_UPDATE while apply defaults to false (:1479-1481); verified applied:false and unchanged revision.

## Impact
Hosts gating destructive tools prompt users for a read-only proposal, discouraging the skill's "try the router first" guidance.

## Fix
Split into a read-only proposal tool + apply_geometry_patch commit, or annotate non-destructive and document apply:true as mutating.
close_reason: route_connection is now annotated IDEMPOTENT_UPDATE (destructiveHint:false) since its default apply:false mode mutates nothing, and its description says apply:true is the only mutating mode (src/server/tools.ts). Pinned by tests/contracts/tool-annotations.test.ts 'proposes a route without mutating, and is not advertised as destructive' (asserts the advertised annotation plus no saveBpmnFile call and an unchanged revision; fails before on destructiveHint true); the EXPECTED_ANNOTATIONS entry that encoded the old value was updated deliberately.

title: update_element with no changes still bumps the revision and rewrites the file
description:
## Evidence
`update_element {elementId:"UserTask_1"}` -> `Updated element UserTask_1`, revision v13 -> v14 (src/server/handlers.ts:1019-1035; schema at src/server/tools.ts:1257-1272 has no at-least-one-field refinement, unlike update_connection).

## Fix
superRefine requiring at least one of name, properties, defaultFlow; skip the write when the merged result is unchanged.
close_reason: update_element now (a) rejects a call naming no field via a superRefine on the schema ('At least one of name, documentation, properties, or defaultFlow must be updated', src/server/tools.ts) and (b) leaves the file and the revision untouched when the merged result serializes byte-identically: commitMutation gained a skipUnchangedWrite mode used only by SimpleBpmnEngine.updateElement, and the handler reports changed:false with matching before/afterRevision. Pinned by tests/integration/handlers.test.ts 'rejects an update that names no field, and writes nothing when values already match' (fails before). tests/security/request-validation.test.ts validArguments.update_element encoded the old no-field call and was updated to pass a name.

title: update_element_geometry rejections carry no structured code or recovery hint (collisionPolicy / route_connection)
description:
## Evidence
Moving Task_1 by 30px with snap-endpoints -> `Error: Geometry collision rejected for Task_1: Edge MessageFlow_1 segment 0 crosses Task_1` (its own snapped edge; src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:2528). Containment failure -> `Unsafe geometry for Task_3: Task_3 is not contained by SubProcess_1` (:2511). Neither has structuredContent or a recovery hint, unlike the compare-and-set conflicts (src/server/handlers.ts:349-357).

## Fix
Return {code:"geometry_rejected", diagnostics:[…], recovery:"…"} structuredContent naming collisionPolicy:"allow" + route_connection as the intended recovery. Part of the structured-error-codes bead.
close_reason: Geometry rejections now carry structured detail: src/server/handlers.ts splits the single geometry classifier into a collision branch (reason:'collision', objectId, diagnostics:[{message,ids}], collisionPolicyApplies:true, recovery naming route_connection and collisionPolicy "allow") and an invariant branch (reason:'invariant', collisionPolicyApplies:false, recovery that explicitly says collisionPolicy does not waive it and points at resizing the container), plus a containment fallback; 'Geometry patch rejected' is now classified too. Pinned by tests/integration/handlers.test.ts 'reports geometry rejections with a code, the diagnostic, and a policy-aware recovery' (verified fails-before by restoring the old single classifier: reason/collisionPolicyApplies absent). NOTE: the full GeometryDiagnostic array (with its code, e.g. CONTAINMENT_FAILURE) still needs a typed error in SimpleBpmnEngine, which was out of this agent's file ownership; the message text is surfaced instead.

title: Query/geometry tools return pretty-printed JSON text that duplicates structuredContent, plus redundant position/size/bounds and repeated waypoints
description:
## Evidence
Every query/geometry tool does textToolResult(name, result, JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)) (src/server/handlers.ts:906, :957, :1000, :1016): the payload is sent twice, once 2-space indented. Each list_elements row carries position, size, and bounds with identical values (:879-895). route_connection repeats the same waypoints in proposedWaypoints, rankedDiagnostics[0].waypoints, and geometryPatch.connectionUpdates[0].waypoints. validate returns each issue twice (issues + errors/warnings).

## Impact
2-3x token cost per call; thousands of tokens for a 100-element page.

## Fix
Compact JSON in the text block (or a short human summary); drop position/size when bounds is present; keep only issues in validate; reference the chosen route by rank.
close_reason: Cut duplicated payload from query/geometry responses: every text block that mirrored structuredContent is now compact JSON via compactJson() instead of 2-space-indented (still complete and parseable, so tests/e2e assertLegacyContent's JSON.parse contract holds); list_elements rows emit position/size only when the row has no DI bounds; validate returns just issues (each carrying its own severity) with errors/warnings dropped from the result and outputSchema; route_connection adds selectedRank and omits that entry's waypoints, which stay in proposedWaypoints and geometryPatch. Pinned by tests/integration/handlers.test.ts 'keeps query and geometry text compact and free of duplicated payload' (fails before). Deliberately updated assertions that encoded the duplication: handlers.test.ts validate tests (validation.errors/.warnings), tests/unit/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.test.ts (row size -> bounds), tests/e2e/server.test.ts validate block. get_element keeps position/size (single-element detail view, and the e2e reads them).

title: Dead Mermaid converter surface: canConvert, analyze, unused ConversionOptions and AST fields
description:
## Evidence
src/converters/MermaidConverter.ts:71-76, :196-271, :315-325: no caller of canConvert/analyze outside the converter and unit tests; handlers call convert(mermaidCode) with no options; includeDataObjects/preview are never read; validateOutput never passed. identifyUnsupportedFeatures uses raw substring checks (includes('click'), includes('style ')), harmless only because unreachable. src/converters/ASTTypes.ts:15-25, :33, :40: MermaidNode.shape/style/position, MermaidEdge.style, MermaidSubgraph.subgraphs are never populated; cleanupNodes filters '|' which \w+ ids cannot contain; the generator's nested-subgraph guard (src/core/SimpleBpmnGenerator.ts:218-226, :49-51) is unreachable.

## Fix
Expose analyze via a preview tool (see the preview bead) or delete it along with the unused options and fields.
close_reason: Removed the genuinely phantom surface: ConversionOptions.includeDataObjects and preview (declared, never read), and MermaidNode.shape/style/position plus MermaidEdge.style (never populated; the parser builds nodes as {id,type,label}). Kept canConvert and analyze deliberately: they are exercised by 34 assertions across two suites that check convert, canConvert and analyze report diagnostics consistently, and preview_mermaid (mcp-bpmn-j21.11) does not consume them, so deleting them now means rewriting working tests rather than removing dead ones. That decision is tracked in mcp-bpmn-iqa.12.

title: Mermaid: add a preview/dry-run tool and conventions to steer node mapping (gateway type, task type, event type)
description:
## Evidence
new_from_mermaid (src/server/tools.ts:917-947) always replaces the current context; there is no way to see the node->BPMN-type mapping, inferred start/end, or sequence-vs-message classification before committing. No Mermaid construct yields a parallel/inclusive gateway, user/service task, or message start event, so each needs a follow-up update_element (which cannot change type either). :::class annotations are already parsed and warned about (src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:400-422) and are a natural hook. The tool description does not mention the supported subset.

## Fix
(1) preview_mermaid returning per-node/per-edge mapping plus diagnostics without touching context; (2) documented conventions e.g. {{…}} -> parallel gateway, ([…]) -> event, :::user / :::service -> task subtype; (3) reference the subset doc in the tool description.
close_reason: Added preview_mermaid: a READ_ONLY dry-run tool that converts Mermaid in memory (autoLayout off) and reports processName, nodeCount/flowCount, per-node {mermaidId, elementId, BPMN type, name, ownerId}, per-edge {connectionId, sequence-vs-message type, endpoints, label}, the pools each subgraph produced, and the conversion warnings, without creating a diagram, writing a file, or replacing the current context (src/server/tools.ts schema+description documenting the supported subset and the constructs Mermaid cannot express; src/server/handlers.ts previewMermaid, which reads the conversion back through BpmnDocumentSerializer). Pinned by tests/integration/handlers.test.ts 'previews the Mermaid mapping without touching the current diagram' and 'previews a failing Mermaid conversion as an error, still without changing context' (fail before: unknown tool), plus an e2e call and a README '#### preview_mermaid' section. NOT DONE: part (2) of the bead, new steering conventions ({{...}} -> parallel gateway, :::user/:::service task subtypes, event shapes) — those need src/converters/MermaidParser.ts and src/utils/TypeMappings.ts, which are owned by another agent in this batch.

title: Mermaid direction (TD/LR/BT/RL) has no effect on the produced diagram but is documented as supported
description:
## Evidence
The same diagram with TD/LR/BT/RL yields byte-identical <bpmndi:BPMNDiagram> on the default path (src/converters/MermaidConverter.ts:144-174; src/core/layout/BpmnLayoutAdapter.ts:104 takes no direction). MermaidAstLayoutAdapter's direction logic (:199-211) is reachable only with autoLayout:false, which no tool passes. skills/bpmn-modeler/references/capabilities.md:63 lists all five directions as supported input.

## Fix
Document that direction is accepted but layout is always LR, or emit a warning when direction != LR, until auto_layout gains a direction option (see the layout-options bead).
close_reason: Fixed with mcp-bpmn-9sv.15: MermaidConverter now maps TD/TB/BT onto the new top-to-bottom layout orientation and LR/RL onto left-to-right, transposing the laid-out document rather than ignoring the declaration. BT and RL read back to front, which BPMN cannot express, so they are laid out forwards and reported in the conversion warnings. capabilities.md and the README state the actual mapping. Pinned by tests/unit/core/LayoutOrientation.test.ts.

title: Mermaid: edge-ID allocator collides with node IDs ending in _N ('A_to_B_2' vs node B_2) and rejects valid input
description:
## Evidence
`A((Start)) --> B\n A --> B\n A --> B_2` (valid) -> `4:5 [DUPLICATE_EDGE] Duplicate Mermaid edge ID: A_to_B_2`; conversion rejected (src/converters/MermaidParser.ts:333-342, :528-537).

## Fix
Allocate edge_<ordinal> (or use a separator that \w+ IDs cannot contain); DUPLICATE_EDGE then becomes unreachable.
close_reason: allocateEdgeId now joins the occurrence suffix with '-' (A_to_B-2) instead of '_'; node IDs match \w+ so a suffixed edge ID can never equal another edge's base ID, and the now-unreachable DUPLICATE_EDGE check plus its ParseErrorCode member were removed. Pinned by tests/unit/converters/MermaidParser.edge-ids.test.ts ('accepts a parallel edge alongside a node whose ID ends in _N', 'never reuses an ID when suffixed and base IDs are interleaved'), which failed with DUPLICATE_EDGE before the change. The 6 legacy A_to_B_2/_3 assertions in tests/unit/converters/MermaidParser.test.ts were updated to the new suffix.

title: engine-contract.md still lists add_lane, validate.level and connect.condition as gaps that are already shipped
description:
## Evidence
docs/architecture/engine-contract.md:51 says add_lane "always returns an implementation error" (G1); :89, :94 say validate.level is ignored and connect.condition is not stored (G5). src/server/handlers.ts:817-825 implements add_lane, :1298-1300 passes level to BpmnValidator, and connect emits `<bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression" language="juel">`.

## Impact
The parity baseline used for release decisions marks shipped features as missing, so reviewers skip testing them.

## Fix
Rewrite G1/G5 as covered; add contract tests for lanes, conditions, and validation levels.

The dependency audit table now lists all nine production deps and the disposition decision is past tense.

title: Dead TypeMappings helpers (createEventDefinition, canConnect, getConnectionType) encode rules that contradict the live engine
description:
## Evidence
src/utils/TypeMappings.ts:12 mapEventType ignores its _eventDefinition parameter; createEventDefinition, canConnect, getConnectionType (:75-127) have no callers in src/. getConnectionType says Participant endpoint => message flow, contradicting the live ownership-based classification in SimpleBpmnEngine.connect.

## Fix
Delete the unused functions and the ignored parameter, or move the mapping tables next to their consumers.
close_reason: Deleted TypeMappings.createEventDefinition, canConnect and getConnectionType (src/utils/TypeMappings.ts:63-118) plus their three describe blocks in tests/unit/utils/TypeMappings.test.ts:64-124. Zero src/ callers (only handlers.ts uses mapEventType/mapActivityType/mapGatewayType, which stay). getConnectionType's 'Participant endpoint => MessageFlow' rule contradicted the live owner/scope classification in SimpleBpmnEngine.connect (SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:820-855). title: Validator does not require an event definition on boundary and intermediate catch events
description:
## Evidence
EVENT_DEFINITION_RULES (src/core/BpmnValidator.ts:462-474) restricts which definitions are allowed but zero definitions always pass. `add_event {eventType:"intermediate-catch", name:"Wait"}` succeeds and validate full reports only missing-flow warnings; an imported boundary event without a definition also passes.

## Fix
Add BPMN_MISSING_EVENT_DEFINITION for bpmn:BoundaryEvent / bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent with no definitions and no eventDefinitionRef; consider requiring eventDefinition for intermediate-catch in add_event.
close_reason: New error BPMN_MISSING_EVENT_DEFINITION in BpmnValidator.validateEvents for bpmn:BoundaryEvent / bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent with no eventDefinitions and no eventDefinitionRef. Pinned by the two new ruleCases entries in tests/unit/core/BpmnValidator.test.ts (Boundary_NoDefinition, Catch_NoDefinition, each with a legal twin) plus the 'BPMN_MISSING_EVENT_DEFINITION' describe covering a root-level eventDefinitionRef and bare start/end/throw events.

title: Import rejects schema-valid bpmn:dataObjectReference variants (absent dataObjectRef, DataObject in an enclosing scope)
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:2358-2377, :2036-2038 assertImportedDataObjectReferences throws when dataObjectRef is absent (the attribute is use="optional" in the XSD) and when the bpmn:dataObject lives in an enclosing scope: `Data object reference dor crosses data object scope`; `… has an invalid dataObjectRef`.

## Fix
Allow absent dataObjectRef (treat as opaque/unmanaged); accept a DataObject whose scope is an ancestor of the reference's scope.
close_reason: BpmnDocument.assertImportedDataObjectReferences now treats an absent dataObjectRef as an opaque reference and accepts a bpmn:DataObject declared in an enclosing scope (new isVisibleDataObjectScope ancestor walk); applyDataObjectReferenceProperties serializes such a reference back without the attribute. Pinned by tests/integration/import-roundtrip.test.ts 'schema-valid data object reference variants', which also keeps the sibling-scope rejection.

title: Validator warns about missing incoming/outgoing flows on event subprocesses and start/end events on ad-hoc subprocesses
description:
## Evidence
src/core/BpmnValidator.ts:655-673, :637-654: a valid event subprocess gets BPMN_PROFILE_MISSING_INCOMING_FLOW / MISSING_OUTGOING_FLOW; ad-hoc subprocesses get BPMN_PROFILE_MISSING_START_EVENT / END_EVENT. The validator also errors when an event subprocess has sequence flows, so the guidance contradicts itself.

## Fix
Skip triggeredByEvent nodes in incoming/outgoing checks; skip bpmn:AdHocSubProcess in start/end checks.
close_reason: BpmnValidator.validateExecutableProfile now skips triggeredByEvent subprocess nodes in the incoming/outgoing checks and skips bpmn:AdHocSubProcess scopes in the start/end checks, so the profile no longer asks for wiring BPMN_EVENT_SUBPROCESS_HAS_SEQUENCE_FLOW forbids. Pinned by tests/unit/core/BpmnValidator.test.ts 'executable profile guidance' (two no-warning cases plus two twins that still flag an ordinary disconnected subprocess and an ordinary subprocess scope).

title: Layout subprocess runner uses falsy short-circuit for error.code — can silently drop real error codes
description: The inline runner script in BpmnAutoLayoutV2Adapter.loadSelectedLayoutInSubprocess (src/core/layout/BpmnLayoutAdapter.ts:209) uses the expression 'error && error.code || "LAYOUT_FAILED"'. If error.code is 0, false, null, or any other falsy non-undefined value, the expression silently falls back to 'LAYOUT_FAILED' and the real error code is lost. Downstream callers (BpmnLayoutError, normalizeLayoutError) that switch on error.code will miss the actual cause. Replace with nullish coalescing: error?.code ?? 'LAYOUT_FAILED' (and similarly for error.message on line 211).
close_reason: The two expressions the bead named were already nullish (BpmnLayoutAdapter.ts:223,225: error?.code ?? 'LAYOUT_FAILED' and error?.message ?? String(error)). Completed the same cleanup on the two remaining falsy short-circuits in the runner: 'elementId: error && error.elementId' -> 'error?.elementId' and 'relatedElementIds: error && error.relatedElementIds' -> 'error?.relatedElementIds' (both would yield the falsy error itself rather than undefined when a non-object is thrown). Added behavioral coverage in tests/unit/layout/BpmnLayoutAdapter.test.ts: 'keeps a present-but-falsy error code out of the unrelated-fallback path' (code: 0 through the public layout() reject path, asserting the raw code survives on cause) and 'preserves a present-but-falsy warning code as a deterministic diagnostic' (code 0 and '' through the warning path), and tightened the source-contract test to assert all four nullish forms and to fail on any 'error && error.elementId' or 'error.code ||' regression.

title: Math.min/max spread pattern over mapped arrays is fragile — fails if arrays exceed ~65k items
description: Several layout functions spread a mapped array directly into Math.min/Math.max: calculateLayoutBounds (src/core/layout/LayoutModel.ts:245-248), updateContainerBounds/layoutWithPools in LayoutEngine (src/core/LayoutEngine.ts:82-87, 264-267), findMinPossibleLevel (LayoutEngine.ts:222-223), normalizeGeometry in bpmnGeometry (tests/helpers/bpmnGeometry.ts:194-203). Node.js throws 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' when more than ~65k arguments are spread. Current resource limits (maxLayoutElements=2000) keep actual counts well below this threshold, but the pattern is a silent footgun: any operator raising the limit above ~32k elements would hit the crash. All spread-into-Math calls should be replaced with .reduce() or equivalent iteration.
close_reason: Verified fixed; no spread-into-Math remains over any caller-influenced array. Repo-wide grep for 'Math.(min|max)(\s*\(\s*\.\.\.|\.apply)' now matches only tests/unit/core/LayoutOrientation.test.ts:157-161, which maps a hardcoded 3-node Mermaid diagram (fixed size, not caller-influenced). Of the cited sites: LayoutModel.calculateLayoutBounds is an accumulator loop (LayoutModel.ts:233-264); src/core/LayoutEngine.ts no longer exists, taking updateContainerBounds/layoutWithPools/findMinPossibleLevel with it; tests/helpers/bpmnGeometry.ts is now a one-line re-export and normalizeGeometry (src/core/BpmnGeometry.ts:425-440) is likewise accumulator-based. Both large-array proof tests exist and pass: 'calculates bounds for more elements than can be passed as function arguments' (150,000 map entries, tests/unit/core/LayoutModel.test.ts:418) and 'normalizes more waypoints than can be passed as function arguments' (150,000 waypoints, tests/helpers/bpmnGeometry.test.ts:223).

title: Add MCP output schemas and structuredContent for machine-readable tool results
description:
## What / impact
Query tools serialize JSON into text blocks and mutation/creation tools return human prose only. No tool declares `outputSchema` or returns `structuredContent`, despite SDK support. MCP clients and agents must scrape strings to obtain generated IDs, filenames, counts, validation issues, and pagination metadata, which is brittle and prevents schema-driven composition.

## Evidence
The tools mapping at src/server/tools.ts:671-675 sets only inputSchema; handlers return `content` but never `structuredContent`. list/get/current/validate already construct JSON objects before stringifying, while new/add/connect results omit stable machine-readable IDs.

## Where
- src/server/tools.ts ToolDefinition/mapping
- src/server/handlers.ts every CallToolResult construction
- src/types/index.ts public result shapes
- contract/e2e tools/list and tools/call assertions

## Implementation direction
Define minimal per-tool output schemas beside input schemas and return the same object in `structuredContent`; retain text content for compatibility. Start with query/export metadata and all creation/mutation tools where generated identifiers are required for subsequent calls. Keep binary/embedded SVG content in MCP content while exposing safe metadata structurally. Validate outputs in tests or a shared boundary.

## Verification
For every advertised tool, call the real server and validate structuredContent against outputSchema, including defaults, pagination, validation issues, generated IDs, XML/SVG metadata, and error responses. Confirm existing text-only clients continue to receive useful content.
acceptance_criteria: Machine-readable tools declare JSON outputSchema and return matching structuredContent while retaining compatible text content; creation/mutation responses expose generated IDs and active filenames; errors remain protocol-compliant; schema/result parity is exhaustively tested through real tools/call responses.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: added validated output schemas and structuredContent for all MCP tools with exhaustive real-server contract coverage

title: Publish accurate MCP tool behavior annotations
description:
## What / impact
All 25 MCP tools are advertised with only name, description, and inputSchema. The installed MCP SDK supports standard behavior annotations, but none are present. Clients therefore cannot accurately distinguish read-only queries from auto-saving mutations and destructive file deletion/overwrite, degrading approval UX and safety policy integration.

## Evidence
`tools` is mapped at src/server/tools.ts:671-675 without `annotations`. Local SDK `Tool` types support `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, and `openWorldHint`. Mutators autosave to disk, while current/list/get/validate/export/get-path are read-only and delete_diagram_file is destructive.

## Where
- src/server/tools.ts toolDefinitions and export mapping
- src/server/handlers.ts actual side effects
- tools/list schema contract tests and README MCP integration notes

## Implementation direction
Make annotations part of each tool definition so advertisement and runtime ownership stay in one source of truth. Review semantics rather than bulk-defaulting: mark reads, local closed-world behavior, idempotency, and destructive operations according to actual filesystem effects. Revisit values when the overwrite/data-loss contract is fixed.

## Verification
Add an exhaustive table over every ToolName with expected annotations and selected behavioral probes (repeat idempotent calls, assert no writes for read-only calls, classify delete). Inspect a real tools/list response through the packed server.
acceptance_criteria: Every advertised tool has reviewed readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint values matching actual persistence and external-I/O behavior; delete/overwrite and read-only operations are classified correctly; a parity test fails when a tool lacks or contradicts annotations; docs explain hints are advisory.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: published reviewed MCP behavior hints for all 27 tools, added exhaustive behavioral parity tests and packed tools/list verification, and documented advisory semantics

title: Add error-path tests for getElement/updateElement/deleteElement with non-existent IDs
description:

title: No tool to add BPMN associations (linking annotations/data objects to elements)
description:
## What
BPMN 2.0 supports bpmn:Association to link elements to text annotations/data objects, but no MCP tool exists to create one and SimpleBpmnEngine has no rendering support.

## Where
src/server/tools.ts (no such tool); src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts (no support).

## Implementation
- Add association as a distinct artifact edge kind, not sequence/message flow.
- Use associationDirection enum None|One|Both with documented default.
- Validate BaseElement endpoints and compatible containing scope.
- Support list/get/delete and DI routing.
- Make text-annotation association delegate to this primitive; do not conflate data input/output associations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Association semantic owner, refs, direction, and DI parse with bpmn-moddle.
- Invalid scopes/endpoints reject before mutation.
- Annotation linking uses the same implementation and deletion behavior is defined.

## Verification
- Run `npx jest tests/unit/core tests/integration/handlers.test.ts --runInBand` for the focused files introduced or named by this bead.
- Run `npm run type-check`.
- After mcp-bpmn-33g.2 closes, run `npm run clean && npm run check` from a checkout with no pre-existing `dist/`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Association semantic owner, refs, direction, and DI parse with bpmn-moddle.
- Invalid scopes/endpoints reject before mutation.
- Annotation linking uses the same implementation and deletion behavior is defined.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: added scoped BPMN associations with direction, DI, MCP query/delete support, and annotation cascade tests

title: No schema-valid tool or Mermaid conversion path for BPMN data objects
description:
## What
No direct data-object tool exists, and the claim that Mermaid import already supports it is false: mapped data nodes can fall through to task. Proper BPMN normally needs both dataObject and dataObjectReference linked by dataObjectRef.

## Where
src/server/tools.ts (no such tool); src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts (no direct-creation support).

## Implementation
- Create dataObject plus dataObjectReference; place isCollection on dataObject.
- Use itemSubjectRef rather than invented itemKind.
- Add correct DI shape and import/update/delete preservation.
- Keep data input/output associations separate from generic association scope.
- Fix or explicitly reject corresponding Mermaid data syntax.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Export contains resolved dataObjectRef pair and correct DI.
- Collection/itemSubject semantics round-trip.
- No data node serializes as task.
- Invalid refs reject.

## Verification

- Run `npm run type-check`.
- After mcp-bpmn-33g.2 closes, run `npm run clean && npm run check` from a checkout with no pre-existing `dist/`.
acceptance_criteria:

- Collection/itemSubject semantics round-trip.

- Invalid refs reject.

title: [if hand-rolling] Implement edge-crossing minimization (Sugiyama phase 3)
description:
## What
Crossing minimization belongs after rank/dummy insertion and before final coordinates/routing. Barycentric sweeps optimize adjacent-rank ordering; arbitrary routed-segment intersection loops are not the phase objective.

## Where
src/utils/AutoLayout.ts (applyHorizontalLayout, ~70-154), src/core/EdgeRouter.ts.

## Implementation
- Perform deterministic downward/upward barycentric or median sweeps over ranked nodes and virtual nodes.
- Count crossings from adjacent-rank order; retain stable ID ties.
- Stop after documented iterations or no improvement, then pass order to coordinate assignment.
- Use a fixture with a known reducible initial ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Known fixture crossing count decreases to the documented expected/minimal value.
- Sequential/no-choice layouts remain unchanged.
- Repeated runs are deterministic.
- Performance is measured with a documented benchmark method; nondeterministic wall-clock thresholds are not the sole gate.

## Verification
- Run `npx jest tests/unit/layout tests/integration/layout-candidates.test.ts --runInBand` for the focused files introduced or named by this bead.
- Run `npm run type-check`.
- After mcp-bpmn-33g.2 closes, run `npm run clean && npm run check` from a checkout with no pre-existing `dist/`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Known fixture crossing count decreases to the documented expected/minimal value.
- Sequential/no-choice layouts remain unchanged.
- Repeated runs are deterministic.
- Performance is measured with a documented benchmark method; nondeterministic wall-clock thresholds are not the sole gate.

title: No support for multi-instance (loop) activity markers
description:

## Where

## Implementation

- Serialize nested FormalExpressions and distinguish standard loop characteristics.
- Validate supported activities/incompatible combinations.
- Treat expression bodies as opaque text with documented language/profile.

## Implementation

title: Remove no-op pipe-character checks in MermaidParser
description:
## What
lines ~134 and ~148 of src/converters/MermaidParser.ts check `!source.includes('|')` / `!target.includes('|')` before parsing, but source/target at that point come from parseEdge() which never includes pipe characters (pipes belong to the separately-extracted label syntax) — these conditions are always true and add confusing dead branching.

## Where
src/converters/MermaidParser.ts (~lines 134, 148).

## Implementation
- After mcp-bpmn-7jf lands, add public parse regressions for A -->|Yes| B and A -.->|No| B with shaped endpoints.
- Remove the always-true pipe guards only; do not alter label extraction or fallback parsing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Labeled normal/dotted edges preserve endpoint IDs, shapes, labels, and edge types.
- No behavior change outside removal of unreachable guards.

## Verification
- Run `npx jest tests/unit/converters --runInBand` for the focused files introduced or named by this bead.
- Run `npm run type-check`.
- After mcp-bpmn-33g.2 closes, run `npm run clean && npm run check` from a checkout with no pre-existing `dist/`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Labeled normal/dotted edges preserve endpoint IDs, shapes, labels, and edge types.
- No behavior change outside removal of unreachable guards.
